https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/head.title: 920249 editorial why the us midterm elections matter
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/head.summary: On Tuesday, 3 November, Americans will vote in what is known as the midterm elections. Historically, midterm elections have been difficult for the president’s party. Indeed, over the last 22 US midterm elections, from 1934 to 2022, the president’s party gained seats in the House of Representatives in only three elections.
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/head.summary_zh: 11月3日星期二，美国选民将参加所谓的期中选举。历史上，期中选举对总统所属政党而言往往十分艰难。事实上，从1934年至2022年的22次美国期中选举来看，总统所属政党仅在3次选举中增加了众议院席位。
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/head.body: On Tuesday, 3 November, Americans will vote in what is known as the midterm elections. In addition to a slew of elections at the municipal levels and a broad range of citizen and legislatively referred initiatives, voters will have their say on all 435 seats in the United States House of Representatives, 35 of the 100 seats in the United States Senate (including two special elections) and for 36 state governors, amongst others. Yet, the one name that is not on the ballot, that of the US president, looms large over this cycle. Historically, midterm elections have been difficult for the president’s party. Indeed, over the last 22 US midterm elections, from 1934 to 2022, the president’s party gained seats in the House of Representatives in only three elections. It lost House seats in the other nineteen. The polls, as of 16 October, give Democrats a 90 per cent chance of winning the House and a 63 per cent chance of controlling the Senate. These predictions are par for the course. The problem is that up until these elections, the Donald Trump presidency has opted to alter courses in unpredictable, if not outrightly illegal ways. Ignore his failed insurrection on 6 January, 2021, and from inciting gerrymanders in Republican-controlled states, to trying to insert the US Postal Services into election processes that are constitutionally state bailiwicks, the Trump administration has been a force for chaos. Its economics, especially the president’s obsession with tariffs, have hurt Americans while strengthening China. His love of tyrant-leaders has seen him cozy up to dictators in North Korea and Russia. In taking up the dictatorship in Iran, in a war whose goals remain as clear as the president’s thinking, he unintentionally handed leverage on the global economy to one of its pariah states, and helped include Israel in a listing of infamous regimes worldwide. To think that all of these were aimed at Making America Great Again (MAGA). While accounting for about 26 per cent of the global economy just before the beginning of the second Trump presidency, America was never a tiddler. Yet, the MAGA quest for further US greatness has seen the US gut much of the infrastructure that has held the global system together during the interwar years. PREMIUM TIMES recognises that from the United Nations through to the many agencies that have been critical to maintaining world peace over the years, the world needs to think differently about how it will be organised over the next one hundred years. The challenges are as onerous as they have always been. The AI revolution and the growing belief in the might-is-right view of international relations only complicate this task further. This newspaper is also aware that much of the thinking for the redesign of the global architecture has already been done by the agencies entrusted with this responsibility. The missing ingredient is the whimsical bent of the leaders of the world’s leading countries. These whimsies, alas, have been lent wings by the capricious Trump administration over the last two years. Will the next Congress keep or lose its ability to check Trump’s policies? In Africa, as the concerns over the administration’s evisceration of the World Health Organisation (WHO) indicates, this is already a major policy conundrum. As if muzzling the WHO were not enough, the Trump administration’s use of aid as a political lever, continues to put Africa in deficit. One can admit that aid is a sovereign US choice, while objecting to its being used to humiliate and punish. The incumbent US federal government tied its decision to end the President’s Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR) support for South Africa to an executive order accusing the country of discriminating against white Afrikaners. Congress has been the backstop before. A similar effort by the administration to claw back unspent PEPFAR funds as part of a wider cut to foreign aid, was stymied by Republican defections in Congress. A renewal of the Trump majority would weaken this backstop. Opposition from the White House and conservative Republicans created an additional vulnerability for the continent when Speaker Mike Johnson was forced to cut the House’s initial renewal of the African Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA) from three to one year. The US trade preference programme enacted in 2000, which provides duty‑free access to the US market for over 1,800 products from eligible sub‑Saharan African countries, has been kept alive until 31 December, after Trump signed a law extending AGOA by one year. This means the next Congress would decide the programme’s future almost immediately. A Republican Congress aligned with the White House is more likely to turn AGOA, whose effectiveness is already weakened by the administration’s rash of tariffs, into a “reciprocity” bargaining chip. South Africa, for example, may have kept its AGOA eligibility, but the 30 per cent “reciprocal” tariffs imposed in 2025 largely cancel its benefits. There are, no doubt, few benefits to the continent from America’s collective ban on mobility. Thirty-six of Africa’s 54 countries now face either US travel bans or visa bonds. This disproportionately hurts students, professionals, diaspora ties, and remittances. While these measures are outcomes of executive orders issued by the White House, congressional oversight and appropriations shape how far they can go. The outcome of the midterm elections will also bear on where deportees go. An AFP investigation found that Washington used the threats of tariffs, visa suspensions, or aid cuts to compel African countries into accepting deportees. Burundi recently became the 15th African nation to agree to this arrangement. The harm here is not only to migrants. As one analysis puts it, these secret deals set precedents that erode the rule of law and transparency that African democracies so sorely need. Congressional scrutiny is one of the few ways these terms become public. A Congress that holds hearings and demands evidence is a check on policy driven by information disorder. A compliant one is not. This matters most when much of the measures taken by the US administration against South Africa draw on “genocide” framings that the two governments reject and that many analysts consider distorted. Because war powers are essentially congressional powers, the US Congress’ willingness to question an expansive reading of a 2001 counterterrorism law will offer African states far more protection from the Trump administration’s penchant for unilateral action. For Nigeria, this is the sharpest issue. Strikes in northwest Nigeria in December were the first US military strikes ever in the country, authorised under the 2001 Authorisation for Use of Military Force Act. Built, as it is, on bogus and false narratives, the Trump administration has been an ill-wind that has served the world poorly over the last 24 months. This is why, PREMIUM TIMES looks forward to a return of a Democratic majority in the US House of Representatives, and hopefully, in the Senate, too
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/head.title_zh: 920249社论：美国中期选举为何至关重要
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/head.body_zh: 11月3日星期二，美国将举行所谓的期中选举。除了一系列市政层级选举以及广泛的公民提案和立法机构转交提案外，选民还将决定美国众议院全部435个席位、美国参议院100个席位中的35席（包括两场特别选举），以及36个州州长等职位。然而，在这一选举周期中，唯一没有出现在选票上的名字——美国总统——却投下了巨大的阴影。历史上，期中选举对总统所属政党而言往往十分艰难。事实上，在美国过去22次期中选举中，从1934年至2022年，总统所属政党仅在3次选举中增加了众议院席位，其余19次均失去席位。截至10月16日的民意调查，民主党赢得众议院控制权的概率为90%，控制参议院的概率为63%。这些预测并不令人意外。问题在于，在此次选举之前，唐纳德·特朗普总统选择了以难以预测、甚至公然违法的方式改变政策路线。先不提他在2021年1月6日失败的叛乱，从煽动共和党控制的州实施选区重划，到试图将美国邮政署纳入宪法上属于各州管辖的选举程序，特朗普政府始终是一股制造混乱的力量。其经济政策，尤其是总统对关税的痴迷，伤害了美国人，却壮大了中国。他对暴君领袖的喜爱，使他与朝鲜和俄罗斯的独裁者沆瀣一气。在对伊朗采取独裁压制并发动一场目标与总统思维一样含混不清的战争时，他无意中将全球经济中的谈判筹码拱手交给了全球最受孤立的国家之一，还帮助把以色列列入全球声名狼藉政权的名单。难以想象，这一切竟然是为了实现“让美国再次伟大”（MAGA）。在特朗普第二任期开始前夕，美国约占全球经济的26%，从来都不是一个无足轻重的国家。然而，“让美国再次伟大”的追求，已使美国掏空了战间期维系全球体系的大量基础设施。PREMIUM TIMES认识到，从联合国到多年来对维护世界和平至关重要的众多机构，世界都需要重新思考未来一百年应如何组织自身。挑战一如既往地艰巨。人工智能革命，以及越来越多人相信国际关系中强权即真理的观点，只会使这项任务更加复杂。本报也知道，重新设计全球架构的许多思路，实际上已经由受托承担这一责任的机构完成。缺少的要素，是世界主要国家领导人异想天开的奇思妙想。可惜的是，过去两年，特朗普政府任性妄为，为这些奇思妙想助长了翅膀。下一届国会会保留还是失去制约特朗普政策的能力？在非洲， administration's 对世界卫生组织（WHO）的削弱所引发的担忧表明，这已经是一个重大的政策难题。仿佛让世卫组织噤声还不够，特朗普政府把援助当作政治杠杆，继续令非洲陷入亏空。人们可以承认援助是美国的主权选择，同时反对将援助用于羞辱和惩罚。美国现任联邦政府把终止“总统艾滋病紧急救援计划”（PEPFAR）对南非支持的决定，与一道指控南非歧视白人南非荷兰人的行政命令挂钩。国会在过去一直是最后的保障。特朗普政府也曾试图追回尚未使用的PEPFAR资金，并将其纳入更广泛的对外援助削减计划，但因共和党议员在国会中倒戈而受阻。特朗普阵营若重新取得多数席位，这一保障将被削弱。白宫和共和党保守派的反对，也令非洲大陆面临更多风险；众议院议长迈克·约翰逊被迫将众议院最初提出的《非洲增长与机会法案》（AGOA）续期从三年缩短至一年。这项于2000年颁布的美国贸易优惠计划，为符合条件的撒哈拉以南非洲国家超过1,800种产品提供免关税进入美国市场的待遇；在特朗普签署将AGOA延长一年的法律后，该计划被保留至12月31日。这意味着，下一届国会几乎会立即决定该计划的未来。与白宫立场一致的共和党国会，更有可能把AGOA变成“互惠”谈判的筹码；其成效已经因政府接连推出关税而受到削弱。例如，南非或许仍保有AGOA资格，但2025年加征的30%“对等”关税在很大程度上抵消了它享有的好处。毫无疑问，美国全面限制人员流动给非洲大陆带来的好处寥寥无几。非洲54个国家中，如今已有36个面临美国旅行禁令或签证保证金要求。这对留学生、专业人士、侨民联系以及汇款造成了不成比例的伤害。尽管这些措施是白宫行政命令的结果，国会的监督和拨款决定着它们能够实施到什么程度。期中选举的结果还将影响被驱逐者的去向。法新社的一项调查发现，华盛顿利用关税威胁、暂停签证或削减援助等手段，迫使非洲国家接收被驱逐者。布隆迪最近成为第15个同意这一安排的非洲国家。这里的伤害不只涉及移民。正如一份分析所指出的，这些秘密协议树立了破坏法治和透明度的先例，而非洲民主制度恰恰迫切需要法治和透明度。国会审查是这些条件得以公开的少数途径之一。举行听证会并要求提供证据的国会，可以制约由信息混乱驱动的政策；唯唯诺诺的国会则不能。当美国政府针对南非采取的大量措施都援引两国均不接受的“种族灭绝”叙事，而许多分析人士认为这些叙事扭曲事实时，国会监督就尤为重要。由于战争权本质上属于国会权力，美国国会是否愿意质疑对2001年反恐法律的扩张性解读，将为非洲各国提供远多于以往的保护，使其免受特朗普政府单方面行动偏好的侵扰。对尼日利亚而言，这是最为尖锐的问题。12月，尼日利亚西北部遭到袭击，这是美国首次在该国实施军事打击；此次行动依据2001年《军事力量使用授权法案》获得批准。特朗普政府建立在虚假和捏造的叙事之上，过去24个月里始终是一股令世界深受其害的逆风。正因如此，PREMIUM TIMES期待美国众议院重新由民主党占据多数，并希望参议院也能如此

https://moderndiplomacy.eu/2026/10/26/ho.title: How Did Myanmar Hide Iranian Jet Fuel Imports to Evade US Sanctions?
https://moderndiplomacy.eu/2026/10/26/ho.summary: Myanmar’s military-linked energy network disguised Iranian jet fuel shipments as South African diesel, using false trade documents and misleading shipping records to conceal transactions worth millions of dollars. The scheme allowed fuel to continue reaching Myanmar despite US sanctions targeting its military’s aviation fuel supply. In December 2025, the tanker Reef , carrying approximately 113,000 barrels of Iranian jet fuel, arrived in Myanmar under paperwork describing the cargo as South African diesel.
https://moderndiplomacy.eu/2026/10/26/ho.summary_zh: 缅甸军方关联的能源网络使用虚假贸易文件和误导性航运记录，将伊朗航空燃料伪装成南非柴油，掩盖了价值数百万美元的交易。尽管美国实施旨在切断缅甸军方航空燃料供应的制裁，这套做法仍使燃料继续运入缅甸。2025年12月，油轮Reef号运载约113,000桶伊朗航空燃料抵达缅甸，相关文件将货物描述为南非柴油。
https://moderndiplomacy.eu/2026/10/26/ho.body: Myanmar’s military-linked energy network disguised Iranian jet fuel shipments as South African diesel, using false trade documents and misleading shipping records to conceal transactions worth millions of dollars. The scheme allowed fuel to continue reaching Myanmar despite US sanctions targeting its military’s aviation fuel supply. In December 2025, the tanker Reef , carrying approximately 113,000 barrels of Iranian jet fuel, arrived in Myanmar under paperwork describing the cargo as South African diesel. A $15.8 million sales contract between Myanmar-based energy broker Dynamic Wave and Thailand’s Tawan-Oil Trading presented the transaction as a legitimate diesel purchase, despite no recorded South African diesel trade with Myanmar in 2025, according to the United Nations and shipping data provider Vortexa. Myanmar’s foreign exchange regulator also appeared to facilitate the arrangement. In a November 30 letter, the regulator reportedly authorized import documents that would label the shipment as diesel rather than jet fuel. The letter also approved payments from Dynamic Wave and its client, National Energy Prime Aviation Services Company, to Tawan. Satellite imagery and shipping analysis by SynMax Intelligence traced the tanker’s journey from Iran’s Bandar Abbas port to Southeast Asia, supporting the conclusion that the cargo originated in Iran. MD Briefing delivers expert analysis across five global fronts — the Indo-Pacific, energy, geoeconomics, European security, and the Middle East — every Monday morning. Free. The United States imposed targeted sanctions on Myanmar’s jet fuel industry in 2023 in response to the military’s air attacks on civilian targets during the country’s ongoing conflict. Purchases of Iranian oil and fuel also expose buyers to US sanctions. Since seizing power in 2021, Myanmar’s military has fought armed resistance groups in a conflict marked by widespread violence and deadly aerial attacks. The United Nations reported in August that military air assaults had killed thousands of people, including civilians. Iran became Myanmar’s primary jet fuel supplier between October 2024 and December 2025, with shipments carried partly by the tankers Reef and Noble . The continued flow of fuel provides Myanmar with supplies for commercial aviation and military air operations, while generating foreign currency for Tehran. The December delivery was not an isolated incident. In May 2025, Dynamic Wave agreed to purchase approximately 202,000 barrels of purported South African diesel from Tawan under a $26 million contract. However, the fuel specifications in the invoice reportedly matched jet fuel rather than diesel, according to jet fuel expert Joshua Heyne of Washington State University and data from Platts. The stated price was also more than 50% above a global diesel benchmark. Shipping records showed that the tanker Noble arrived in Yangon in June carrying just under 200,000 barrels of jet fuel intended for Dynamic Wave. According to SynMax’s satellite analysis, the vessel loaded its cargo at Bandar Abbas and transmitted location signals that made it appear to be heading towards Chittagong, Bangladesh. These transactions suggest that the network relied on multiple methods to obscure the fuel’s origin and destination, including misleading contracts, mislabelled import documents and deceptive shipping signals. The contracts directed payments to Tawan’s account at Siam Commercial Bank (SCB), Thailand’s oldest bank. A 2024 report by United Nations experts had identified Tawan as a jet fuel supplier to Myanmar’s military and described SCB as a major facilitator of military procurement. SCB previously stated that it complied with anti-money-laundering laws and that its Myanmar-related transactions were legitimate and unrelated to the arms trade. Reuters could not establish whether the bank knew the nature of Tawan’s business. Thai regulators had ordered banks in 2024 to scrutinize Myanmar-related transactions more closely to comply with sanctions and anti-money-laundering requirements. SCB, Tawan and the Bank of Thailand did not respond to Reuters’ latest requests for comment. The case highlights both the reach and limitations of US economic sanctions. The apparent need to disguise Iranian jet fuel as diesel suggests that sanctions have raised the risks associated with these transactions. Yet the continued arrival of Iranian fuel indicates that restrictions have not fully stopped the trade. The transactions also raise questions about the role of intermediaries, import documentation and financial institutions in enforcing sanctions across borders. Even when a government restricts direct purchases, opaque commercial arrangements and misleading shipping records can make it difficult to identify the origin and end use of sensitive goods. Myanmar’s military-linked companies and Iranian suppliers have continued to operate despite these restrictions. Reuters reported in October that Iranian jet fuel shipments to Myanmar were still taking place in 2026. The case therefore illustrates a central challenge for sanctions enforcement: restricting access to strategic supplies requires not only targeting suppliers and buyers but also detecting the commercial and financial mechanisms used to conceal transactions. https://moderndiplomacy.eu/2026/10/26/ho.title_zh: 缅甸如何隐藏伊朗航空燃料进口以规避美国制裁？
https://moderndiplomacy.eu/2026/10/26/ho.body_zh: 缅甸军方关联的能源网络把伊朗航空煤油伪装成南非柴油，使用虚假贸易文件和误导性航运记录，掩盖价值数百万美元的交易。尽管美国实施针对缅甸军方航空燃油供应的制裁，这套网络仍让燃油持续运入缅甸。2025年12月，油轮Reef载有约113,000桶伊朗航空煤油抵达缅甸，相关文件却将货物描述为南非柴油。据联合国和航运数据提供商Vortexa提供的信息，总部位于缅甸的能源经纪商Dynamic Wave与泰国的Tawan-Oil Trading签订了一份价值1,580万美元的销售合同，将这笔交易包装成正常的柴油采购，尽管2025年并无任何南非柴油与缅甸之间的贸易记录。缅甸外汇监管机构似乎也为这一安排提供了便利。据报道，该监管机构在11月30日的一封信中批准了进口文件授权，将这批货物标为柴油而非航空煤油。这封信还批准了Dynamic Wave及其客户National Energy Prime Aviation Services Company向Tawan付款。SynMax Intelligence的卫星图像和航运分析追踪了这艘油轮从伊朗阿巴斯港前往东南亚的航程，支持货物源自伊朗的结论。MD Briefing每周一上午提供印太、能源、地缘经济、欧洲安全和中东五大全球领域的专家分析。免费。2023年，美国针对缅甸航空煤油行业实施定向制裁，以回应军方在该国持续冲突期间对民用目标发动的空袭。购买伊朗石油和燃油也会使买方面临美国制裁。自2021年夺取政权以来，缅甸军方一直与武装抵抗组织交战，冲突伴随大范围暴力和致命空袭。联合国8月报告称，军方空袭造成数千人死亡，包括平民。2024年10月至2025年12月，伊朗成为缅甸的主要航空煤油供应国，部分货物由Reef和Noble油轮运输。燃油持续流入，为缅甸的商业航空和军事空中行动提供补给，同时为德黑兰创造外汇收入。12月的交付并非孤立事件。2025年5月，Dynamic Wave同意根据一份价值2,600万美元的合同，从Tawan购买约202,000桶所谓的南非柴油。然而，据华盛顿州立大学航空煤油专家Joshua Heyne和Platts的数据，发票所列燃油规格实际上与航空煤油相符，而非柴油。发票标示的价格也比全球柴油基准价格高出50%以上。航运记录显示，油轮Noble于6月抵达仰光，载有略少于200,000桶、拟交付Dynamic Wave的航空煤油。根据SynMax的卫星分析，该船在阿巴斯港装载货物，并发送位置信号，伪装成驶往孟加拉国吉大港。这些交易表明，该网络采用了多种手段掩盖燃油的来源和目的地，包括误导性合同、错标进口文件以及欺骗性航运信号。合同将付款导向Tawan在泰国历史最悠久的银行Siam Commercial Bank（SCB）的账户。联合国专家2024年的一份报告将Tawan认定为缅甸军方的航空煤油供应商，并称SCB是军方采购的重要协助方。SCB此前表示，其遵守反洗钱法律，与缅甸有关的交易合法且与军火贸易无关。路透社无法确定该银行是否知道Tawan业务的实际性质。2024年，泰国监管机构曾命令银行加强审查与缅甸有关的交易，以遵守制裁和反洗钱要求。SCB、Tawan和泰国央行均未回应路透社最新的置评请求。此案凸显了美国经济制裁的覆盖范围及其局限。把伊朗航空煤油伪装成柴油的明显需求表明，制裁提高了这些交易的风险。然而，伊朗燃油仍持续运抵缅甸，说明限制措施尚未完全切断贸易。这些交易也引出了有关中介机构、进口文件和金融机构如何在跨境执行制裁的问题。即使政府限制直接采购，不透明的商业安排和误导性航运记录仍可能使人难以识别敏感货物的来源和最终用途。尽管受到这些限制，缅甸军方关联公司和伊朗供应商仍在继续运营。路透社10月报道称，2026年仍有伊朗航空煤油运往缅甸。因此，此案说明了制裁执行面临的一项核心挑战：要限制战略物资的获取，不仅要针对供应商和买方，还要识别用来掩盖交易的商业和金融机制。MD不支持任何特定议程、叙事或思想流派。我们旨在让所有观点、思想和论点接受审视，并检验其中哪些仍然有效且站得住脚

https://www.thehindu.com/opinion/op-ed/u.body: Account subscription benefits alongside Premium Stories, Editorials, Opinions and more. Unlock these with Subscription In its second term, the Donald Trump administration has been active in restricting legal immigration to the United States. The administration’s attempt to impose a $100,000 payment requirement on certain new H-1B petitions, changes to visa renewal procedures, the introduction of a wage-weighted selection system, and the latest suspensions of the Program Electronic Review Management (PERM) process are cases in point, disproportionately impacting Indian immigrants and firms. It is tempting to read these developments as a product of the Trump administration alone, but they reflect deeper political interests that are likely to survive post-Trump. Indian nationals account for 70% of H-1B visa approvals, with one-fifth of the visas going to employees of Indian-origin companies. This means that, as the bipartisan focus on immigration reform continues, the issue is likely to sustain as a friction point in India-U.S. relations. Democrats are expected to dominate the upcoming midterm elections in November. They view immigration through a rights-based lens, and their voters remain supportive of both legal immigration and increased legalisation of undocumented immigrants. Some 75% of Democrats see skilled immigration as good for the U.S., compared with 54% of Republicans. Even under the current administration, Democrats have pushed for easing F-1 student visa requirements and have traditionally enjoyed the support of diaspora communities in the U.S., including the Indian diaspora. Immigrants seeking U.S. citizenship targeted in Trump administration's illegal voting crackdown U.S. proposes new rule to scrap 60-day grace period for H-1B workers after job loss However, prominent Democratic Senators such as Dick Durbin and Richard Blumenthal, as well as progressive Independents such as Bernie Sanders, have also pushed for bills seeking H-1B reforms. Democrats view alleged fraud in the H-1B visa system as a serious challenge that needs to be addressed. Similarly, the labour wing of the Democratic Party views the H-1B visa programme as a potential threat to domestic labour protections and workers’ rights. The Democrats’ immigrant voter base, their open opposition to the H-1B visa fee hikes, and resistance to these restrictions from businesses and unions suggest that a Democratic-controlled Congress may soften the harshest executive measures and tone down the rhetoric. However, concerns about visa fraud and worker protections mean that Democrats are likely to keep up the pressure on the outsourcing model and continue pushing for H-1B reforms. While a plurality of Republicans support restrictions on legal immigration, this number has declined considerably since 2025. Among the Republican leadership, there is a visible split between anti-immigration nationalists and pro-immigration business interests. The Trump administration’s hikes in the H-1B visa fee is an example of this conflict. While the administration was openly critical of the programme and aggressively pushed for the fee increase, it subsequently diluted the measure by including exemptions for graduates of U.S. universities and existing visa holders, following pressure from businesses and universities. The debate over wage-weighted entries versus the lottery system for H-1B visas has dominated discussions on immigration within the U.S. business community. There are three broad categories in this debate. The first is the random lottery system that was in place until 2026, which benefited outsourcing firms and start-ups. The second is the wage-weighted lottery system (February 2026), which infers wage levels based on experience, job role and location, dividing visa quotas into four categories. On the surface, this system might benefit big-tech firms, but it could also benefit outsourcing firms that hire highly experienced workers for lower wages. The third is the actual wage weighted lottery model, which is supported by U.S.-based industries. This approach could dilute the advantages enjoyed by outsourcing firms while benefiting American hires and also F1 student hires. If India plays its cards right, suspension of PERM may be an opportunity: Priyank Kharge Trump’s move to suspend PERM programme for Indian IT majors raises talent-retention concerns MEA says U.S. green card suspension measures do not advance shared India-U.S. ambitions For the artificial intelligence (AI) and big-tech business community, this reform could be beneficial in two ways. First, AI graduate programmes and advanced research roles in the U.S. rely heavily on international talent, with demand for AI skills growing faster than the supply of domestic graduates. The reform could therefore help AI firms secure top international talent for higher wages. Second, the AI sector is expanding into market segments traditionally occupied by start-ups and outsourcing companies, which often perform low technology maintenance and communication roles. The AI sector could therefore benefit if these start-ups and outsourcing firms were compelled to hire fewer workers. With the AI sector playing a prominent role in campaign contributions for the 2026 midterm elections, these policies to counter outsourcing firms are likely to continue. With over 54% of India’s software services exports going to the U.S., which remains the top market for Indian information technology (IT) outsourcing, this represents a major challenge for India. However, these developments could also be viewed as positive news for Indian students at U.S. universities. The U.S. Department of Labor’s suspension of eight firms, including not only Indian outsourcing companies such as Infosys, Tata Consultancy Services and Wipro but also major technology firms such as Microsoft and Adobe, from green card sponsorship reinforces this trend. It raises the cost of hiring foreign workers for businesses as a whole, creating pressure that remains largely beyond partisan control. With Mr. Trump’s political power potentially diminished after November, anti-immigration rhetoric could decline. However, with both parties committed to immigration reform, India should continue to expect an unfavourable and unpredictable immigration landscape. https://www.thehindu.com/opinion/op-ed/u.title_zh: 美国移民限制措施可能比特朗普任期更长久
https://www.thehindu.com/opinion/op-ed/u.body_zh:
订阅可享受《The Hindu》会员故事、社论、观点等更多内容。订阅即可解锁这些内容。

特朗普政府进入第二个任期以来，积极限制合法移民赴美国。该政府试图对某些新的H-1B申请施加10万美元缴费要求、改变签证续签程序、推出工资加权筛选系统，以及最近暂停项目电子审查管理（PERM）流程，这些都是其典型做法，对印度移民和企业造成了不成比例的影响。人们很容易将这些 developments 解读为特朗普政府单独推出的产物，但它们实际上反映了更深层次的政治利益，而这种利益很可能在特朗普卸任后继续存在。

印度公民占H-1B签证批准人数的70%，其中五分之一的签证发放给了印度裔公司的员工。这意味着，随着两党继续关注移民改革，该问题很可能持续成为印美关系中的摩擦点。预计民主党将在11月即将举行的中期选举中占据优势。他们从权利视角看待移民，其选民仍然支持合法移民以及增加无证移民合法化。约75%的民主党人士认为技术移民有利于美国，而共和党人士的这一比例为54%。即便在现任政府执政期间，民主党也一直主张放宽F-1学生签证要求，并且历来得到美国侨民社群的支持，其中包括印度侨民。

特朗普政府打击非法投票行动所针对的、寻求美国公民身份的移民

美国提议制定新规，取消H-1B工人在失业后的60天宽限期

不过，Dick Durbin和Richard Blumenthal等资深民主党参议员，以及Bernie Sanders等进步派独立人士，也一直在推动旨在改革H-1B的法案。民主党认为，有关H-1B签证系统存在欺诈的指控是一项必须解决的严重挑战。同样，民主党内的劳工派将H-1B签证项目视为对国内劳工保护和工人权利的潜在威胁。

民主党所拥有的移民选民基础、他们对提高H-1B签证费率的公开反对，以及企业和工会对这些限制的抵制，都表明由民主党控制的国会可能会软化最严厉的行政措施，并降低相关言论的强硬程度。

不过，对签证欺诈和劳工保护的担忧意味着，民主党很可能继续向外包模式施压，并继续推动H-1B改革。

虽然多数共和党人士支持限制合法移民，但这一比例自2025年以来已大幅下降。在共和党领导层中，反移民民族主义者与支持移民的商业利益之间出现了明显分化。特朗普政府提高H-1B签证费就是这种冲突的一个例子。该政府公开批评这一项目，并积极推动提高费用，但在企业和大学施加压力后，随后通过为美国大学毕业生和现有签证持有者设置豁免，削弱了该措施的影响。

围绕H-1B签证采用工资加权录取还是抽签制度展开的争论，一直主导着美国商业界的移民讨论。这场争论大致分为三类。第一类是截至2026年一直采用的随机抽签制度，它有利于外包企业和初创公司。第二类是工资加权抽签制度（2026年2月推出），该制度根据工作经验、职位和所在地推定工资水平，将签证配额划分为四个类别。表面上，这套制度可能有利于大型科技公司，但也可能让那些以较低工资聘用经验丰富的员工的外包企业受益。第三类是真正的工资加权抽签模式，得到美国本土行业的支持。这一做法可能削弱外包企业的优势，同时让美国本土招聘和F1学生招聘受益。

如果印度审慎应对，暂停PERM可能是一个机会：Priyank Kharge

特朗普暂停面向印度IT专业人士的PERM项目，引发人才留任担忧

印度外交部表示，美国暂停绿卡措施无助于推进印美共同目标

对于人工智能（AI）和大型科技商业群体而言，这项改革可能带来两方面好处。第一，美国的人工智能研究生项目和高水平研究岗位高度依赖国际人才，而对人工智能技能的需求增长快于本土毕业生供给。因此，这项改革可能帮助人工智能企业以更高薪酬留住顶尖国际人才。第二，人工智能行业正在向传统上由初创公司和外包企业占据的市场领域扩张，而这些企业通常承担低技术维护和沟通工作。因此，如果这些初创公司和外包企业被迫减少招聘，人工智能行业可能从中受益。

鉴于人工智能行业在2026年中期选举的竞选捐款中占据重要地位，这些制衡外包企业的政策很可能会延续下去。印度超过54%的软件服务出口流向美国，而美国仍是印度信息技术（IT）外包的首大市场，因此上述趋势对印度构成重大挑战。

不过，这些 developments 也可以被视为印度学生在美国大学就读的利好消息。美国劳工部暂停八家企业为外籍员工提供绿卡担保，其中包括Infosys、Tata Consultancy Services和Wipro等印度外包企业，也包括Microsoft和Adobe等大型科技企业，这进一步强化了这一趋势。它提高了整个企业群体聘用外国劳工的成本，从而形成一种基本不受党派控制的压力。

如果特朗普先生的政治权力在11月之后可能减弱，反移民言论或许会减少。然而，由于两党都致力于移民改革，印度应继续预期移民环境将处于不利且难以预测的状态。

https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/26/i.body: Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals has reported a sharp increase in investor subscriptions as its landmark Initial Public Offering (IPO) enters its final days, with retail and institutional investors accelerating participation ahead of the closing date of October 27. The company confirmed, in a statement yesterday, that the IPO will close on Tuesday, October 27, as scheduled. The company said, “This is the final deadline, and no further extension will be granted. Investors wishing to participate must complete their subscriptions before the offer closes.” The surge in demand follows the refinery’s recently released nine-month financial results, which showed exceptional growth in revenue, profitability, and cash generation, reinforcing investor confidence in the company’s long-term prospects. Dangote Refinery reported revenue of $22.5 billion and net profit of $4.73 billion for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, representing a significant turnaround from a loss recorded in the corresponding period of 2025. Revenue increased by 144 per cent year-on-year, while Earnings, Interest, Taxes, Depreciation and Amortisation (EBITDA) rose to $5.5 billion, reflecting higher refining throughput, improved operational reliability and stronger refining margins. The company also strengthened its balance sheet, moving from a net debt position to a net cash position during the period. It said the strong financial performance, combined with the refinery’s strategic importance to Africa’s energy security and industrial development, has continued to attract broad-based interest from individual investors, pension funds, institutional investors, asset managers, professionals, business owners and members of the African diaspora. The statement said, “The level of investor interest we are seeing reflects growing confidence in our business and in the strong financial results we have delivered. According to the refinery, the IPO has become more than a capital-raising exercise, evolving into an opportunity for Africans and international investors to participate directly in the ownership of one of the continent’s most significant industrial enterprises. It stated that subscriptions had been received from across Nigeria, other African countries and international markets, underscoring the refinery’s growing reputation as a world-class industrial asset. The company stated, “Investors recognise that this refinery is not merely an energy asset. It is a platform for industrial growth, foreign-exchange generation, regional trade, energy security and economic development across Africa. The company also reiterated its commitment to broad-based ownership, emphasising that the IPO has been structured to ensure that ordinary investors can participate alongside institutional investors in the refinery’s future growth. It advised prospective investors who had not yet completed their subscriptions to do so immediately through their stockbrokers and approved distribution channels before the deadline. It stated, “This is the final opportunity for investors to participate in this historic offer. Dangote refinery expressed appreciation to regulators, issuing houses, stockbrokers, financial institutions, fintech partners, investor associations, market operators, and the investing public for their support throughout the offer period. The company added that the strong demand recorded so far demonstrated growing investor confidence in African-owned industrial enterprises and highlighted the increasing capacity of African capital markets to support large-scale transformational investments. The statement said, “History is being made. The remarkable investor response is a powerful vote of confidence in Africa’s future, in African enterprise, and in the long-term value that world-class industrial projects can create when opened to public ownership. We remain committed to delivering sustained growth and enduring value for all shareholders.” Founded on January 22, 1995, THISDAY is published by THISDAY NEWSPAPERS LTD., 35 Creek Road Apapa, Lagos, Nigeria with offices in 36 states of Nigeria , the Federal Capital Territory and around the world. https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/26/i.title_zh: 丹格特炼油厂股票认购于10月27日截止，投资者蜂拥而至
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/26/i.body_zh:
丹格特石油炼化公司旗下炼油厂表示，随着其具有里程碑意义的首次公开募股进入最后阶段，投资者认购额大幅增加；在10月27日截止日期到来之前，散户和机构投资者均加快了参与步伐。该公司昨天在一份声明中确认，首次公开募股将按计划于10月27日星期二截止。公司表示：“这是最后截止期限，不会再获延期。希望参与的投资者必须在发售截止前完成认购。”

需求激增出现在该炼油厂最近公布的九个月财务业绩之后。相关业绩显示，其收入、盈利能力和现金生成能力均实现突出增长，进一步增强了投资者对公司长期前景的信心。丹格特炼油厂报告，截至2026年9月30日的九个月收入为$22.5 billion，净利润为$4.73 billion，与2025年同期录得的亏损相比实现显著扭转。收入同比增长144 per cent，息税折旧摊销前利润（EBITDA）升至$5.5 billion，反映出炼油加工量提高、运营可靠性增强以及炼油利润率改善。公司还 strengthen 了自己的资产负债表，在报告期内由净债务转为净现金状态。

公司表示，强劲的财务表现，加上该炼油厂对非洲能源安全和工业发展的战略重要性，持续吸引个人投资者、养老基金、机构投资者、资产管理人、专业人士、企业主以及非洲侨民的广泛参与。声明称：“我们看到的投资者参与热度，反映出市场对我们业务以及我们所交付的强劲财务业绩日益增长的信心。

据该炼油厂介绍，此次首次公开募股已超越单纯融资的范畴，正逐步成为非洲人和国际投资者直接参与非洲大陆最具重要意义的工业企业之一所有权的机会。该公司表示，认购资金来自尼日利亚全国、其他非洲国家及国际市场，这凸显了炼油厂作为世界级工业资产日益提升的声誉。

公司表示：“投资者认识到，这座炼油厂不仅是能源资产，也是推动工业增长、外汇创造、区域贸易、能源安全和非洲全境经济发展的平台。公司还重申了对广泛持股的承诺，强调此次首次公开募股的结构旨在确保普通投资者能够与机构投资者一道，参与炼油厂未来的增长。公司建议尚未完成认购的潜在投资者立即通过其证券经纪商和获准的分销渠道完成认购，务必赶在截止期限之前。

公司表示：“这是投资者参与此次历史性发售的最后机会。

丹格特炼油厂向监管机构、承销机构、证券经纪商、金融机构、金融科技合作伙伴、投资者协会、市场运营方及投资公众在整个发售期间给予的支持表示 appreciation。公司补充称，迄今录得的强劲需求证明，投资者对非洲人持股的工业企业日益充满信心，也凸显了非洲资本市场支持大规模转型性投资的不断提升的能力。声明称：“历史正在被创造。投资者热烈响应，是对非洲未来、非洲企业以及向公众开放所有权后世界级工业项目能够创造的长期价值的有力信心投票。我们仍致力于为全体股东实现持续增长和持久价值。”

https://leadership.ng/7-month-petrol-sto.body: Nigeria’s petrol stock cover has remained below the 30-day safety benchmark for seven consecutive months, raising concerns about possible supply constraints towards the end of the year as petroleum marketers reportedly reduce imports amid claims that banks have declined to issue Letters of Credit (LCs) to importers. The concerns come as data from the September 2026 factsheet of the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority (NMDPRA) show declining petrol imports and domestic deliveries ahead of the festive season. According to the factsheet, petrol stock cover stood at 23.9 days in September, up from 22.9 days in August but still 6.1 days below the required 30-day threshold. Stock cover fell from 30.9 days in February to 21.2 days in March, before reaching its lowest point of 16.2 days in May. It has since risen for four consecutive months, increasing to 19.6 days in June, 22.4 days in July, 22.9 days in August and 23.9 days in September. The average stock cover over the seven-month period was approximately 20.6 days. Inland depots accounted for 22.7 days of the September cover, while the NMDPRA’s calculation also included petrol stocks at the Dangote refinery. Despite remaining below the safety benchmark, the September position was better than the corresponding period last year, when stock cover stood at 16.9 days before falling further to 11.1 days in October 2025. However, the pace of recovery has slowed. Stock cover increased by 2.8 days between June and July, but the gains narrowed to 0.5 days in August and one day in September. The concerns follow a 30 per cent decline in petrol imports in September, from 14.6 million litres per day in August to 10.2 million litres per day, as approved import permit volumes were reportedly being exhausted. Total petrol receipts fell by 23 per cent, from 50.5 million litres per day in August to 38.7 million litres per day in September, while consumption increased by seven per cent to 44.4 million litres per day. Domestic petrol receipts also declined by 21 per cent, from 35.9 million litres per day to 28.5 million litres per day. This meant the market received 11.8 million fewer litres of petrol daily in September than in August. The decline occurred despite a 13 per cent increase in petrol production at the Dangote Petroleum Refinery, which raised its average daily output from 41.94 million litres in August to 47.22 million litres in September. The refinery’s average capacity utilisation also increased from 105.21 per cent to 105.98 per cent, above its installed capacity of 650,000 barrels per day. However, the increase in production did not translate into higher domestic deliveries. Dangote’s domestic petrol supply fell by about one-fifth, while its petrol exports rose by 59 per cent, from 9.73 million litres per day in August to 15.47 million litres per day in September. The refinery also added 3.25 million litres per day to its petrol stocks, ending September with 366.2 million litres, compared with 360.4 million litres at the end of August. The reduction in petrol imports has raised concerns about possible supply disruptions, particularly as demand typically increases towards the end of the year. With petrol stock cover remaining below the 30-day benchmark for seven months, analysts fear that a further decline in supplies could trigger domestic shortages as the festive season approaches. However, the Secretary of the Major Energy Marketers Association of Nigeria (MEMAN), Clement Isong, did not immediately provide a specific explanation for the sharp decline in imports by the association’s members. Responding to an enquiry by LEADERSHIP, Isong said: “Let me cross-check and find out. However, I am trying to put your concerns in perspective and come up with proper analysis.” An industry source who also imports petroleum products, however, told LEADERSHIP that some financial institutions had declined to issue Letters of Credit to petroleum marketers. Although the source could not confirm the reasons for the alleged refusals, another industry source claimed that banks were being pressured or coerced into denying importers access to the credit facilities. The Chief Executive Officer of the Centre for the Promotion of Private Enterprise (CPPE), Dr Muda Yusuf, offered a different explanation, suggesting that the decline in imports could be linked to rising crude oil prices, which were around $115 per barrel. “I will say that it’s all about business decisions and also concerns by financial institutions not to run the risk of losing money,” Yusuf said. He explained that businesses and financial institutions had to consider the risks of committing funds to a commodity whose price was volatile. Yusuf also cautioned that ongoing discussions between the United States and Russia could trigger a sudden fall in crude oil prices, potentially leaving importers with substantial losses if they purchased products at higher prices. Meanwhile, the National President of the Petroleum Products Retail Outlets Owners Association of Nigeria (PETROAN), Prince Dr Billy Gillis-Harry, played down fears of possible shortages, saying the NMDPRA had taken steps to safeguard supply. Speaking to LEADERSHIP, he said the regulator had the necessary data to monitor supply and would ensure that any shortfall was addressed through imports or domestic sourcing. Figures from last year illustrate how sharply petrol demand can rise towards the end of the year, potentially putting additional pressure on current stock levels. Petrol consumption, measured by volumes trucked out, increased from 43.8 million litres per day in September 2025 to 56.7 million litres per day in October, peaking at 63.7 million litres per day in December. Consumption in September 2026 stood at 44.4 million litres per day. A return to December 2025 levels would therefore represent an increase of approximately 43 per cent. Last year, petrol stock cover recovered to 29.3 days in December and 33 days in January following increased supplies. Daily receipts reached 71.5 million litres in November and 74.2 million litres in December, including imports of 52.1 million litres and 42.2 million litres per day, respectively. Based on September’s stock cover and consumption figures, current petrol stocks were estimated at approximately 1.06 billion litres. At December 2025’s consumption rate of 63.7 million litres per day, that volume would last about 16.7 days. Maintaining 30 days of stock cover at that level of consumption would require approximately 1.9 billion litres of petrol. Any additional import cargoes would be priced against prevailing market benchmarks. In September, dated Brent crude was quoted at $116.77 per barrel, while the naira traded at N1,327.31 to the dollar. Indicative petrol pump prices ranged from N1,371.01 per litre in Lagos to N1,464.75 per litre in Maiduguri. The supply position for cooking gas, also known as liquefied petroleum gas (LPG), was tighter than that of petrol, with stock cover remaining significantly below the regulatory benchmark. LPG stock cover stood at 15.9 days in September, 14.1 days below the threshold, while consumption was reported at 133.3 per cent of the benchmark. Daily LPG receipts rose by nine per cent to 4.7 kilotonnes, driven by a 50 per cent increase in domestic supply to 4.5 kilotonnes. Imports, however, fell by 85 per cent to 0.2 kilotonnes. Domestic sources accounted for approximately 96 per cent of LPG receipts, while consumption increased by eight per cent to 5.2 kilotonnes per day. In contrast, diesel and aviation fuel maintained stock levels above the safety threshold. Diesel stock cover stood at 49.7 days, while aviation fuel cover was 53.2 days. Despite the relatively comfortable stock position, daily diesel receipts fell by 40 per cent, from 14.5 million litres in August to 8.7 million litres in September, the lowest level recorded in the 13 months covered by the regulator’s data. Domestic diesel receipts declined by 39 per cent, from 13.2 million litres to 8.1 million litres per day, while imports fell by 54 per cent, from 1.3 million litres to 600,000 litres per day. Consumption, however, edged up from 14.3 million litres to 14.5 million litres per day. Dangote’s diesel production increased by 35 per cent to 24.32 million litres per day. However, its domestic deliveries fell from 12.37 million litres to 8.14 million litres per day, while exports rose by 82 per cent, from 8.75 million litres to 15.91 million litres per day. The refinery ended September with 232.5 million litres of diesel in stock, compared with 137.2 million litres at the end of August. 1. The Stock cover is still below safe levels. Petrol cover was 23.9 days in September, 6.1 days short of the 30-day benchmark. It has stayed below that mark for seven straight months. It hit a low of 16.2 days in May and has risen every month since, though the pace of recovery is slowing. 2. Imports are falling. Petrol imports dropped 30 per cent in September, from 14.6 to 10.2 million litres per day, as approved import permit volumes ran out. Total receipts fell 23 per cent to 38.7 million litres per day, while consumption rose 7 per cent to 44.4 million. 3. Dangote is producing more but delivering less locally. The refinery raised output 13 per cent to 47.22 million litres per day, yet its domestic petrol supply fell by about one-fifth. Its petrol exports jumped 59 per cent to 15.47 million litres per day, and it added to its own stock. 4. Why marketers cut imports is disputed. One industry source says banks have declined Letters of Credit to importers. Another alleges banks are being pressured to do so. The reasons are unconfirmed, and MEMAN’s secretary, Clement Isong, did not explain the drop. CPPE’s Dr Muda Yusuf says it is a business decision: crude is about $115 per barrel. 5. The festive season is the real risk. Last year, consumption rose from 43.8 million litres per day in September to 63.7 million in December. A repeat would mean about 43 per cent more demand. At that pace, current stock of about 1.061 billion litres would last only about 16.7 days. Holding 30 days’ cover would need about 1.9 billion litres. We’ve got the edge. https://leadership.ng/7-month-petrol-sto.title_zh: 汽油库存短缺达7个月，引发年末供应担忧
https://leadership.ng/7-month-petrol-sto.body_zh:
尼日利亚汽油库存覆盖天数连续7个月低于30天的安全基准。據报道，石油产品经销商在进口商称银行拒绝开立信用证（LC）之际减少进口，因此市场担心年底前可能出现供应受限。

尼日利亚中游和下游石油监管局（NMDPRA）2026年9月数据显示，在节日季到来前，汽油进口量和国内交付量均在下降。根据该数据，9月汽油库存覆盖天数为23.9天，高于8月的22.9天，但仍比30天的规定门槛低6.1天。库存覆盖天数从2月的30.9天降至3月的21.2天，随后在5月降至最低点的16.2天。此后已连续4个月回升，6月增至19.6天、7月增至22.4天、8月增至22.9天、9月增至23.9天。这7个月的平均库存覆盖天数约为20.6天。9月库存覆盖天数中，内陆油库占22.7天，NMDPRA的计算还计入了Dangote炼油厂的汽油库存。

尽管仍低于安全基准，9月的情况好于去年同期。去年同期库存覆盖天数为16.9天，随后在2025年10月进一步降至11.1天。不过，库存回升速度已经放缓。6月至7月库存覆盖天数增加2.8天，但8月增幅收窄至0.5天，9月仅增加1天。

9月汽油进口量下降30%，从8月每日1460万升降至每日1020万升，据报道，原因是获批进口许可证对应的进口量即将用尽。汽油总接收量下降23%，从8月每日5050万升降至9月每日3870万升，而消费量则增长7%，升至每日4440万升。国内汽油接收量也下降21%，从每日3590万升降至每日2850万升。这意味着9月市场每日获得的汽油比8月少1180万升。

尽管Dangote石油炼油厂的汽油产量增长13%，其平均日产量从8月的4194万升提高至9月的4722万升，汽油进口量仍然下降。该炼油厂的平均产能利用率也从105.21%升至105.98%，高于其每日65万桶的装机产能。然而，产量增加并未转化为国内交付量上升。Dangote面向国内市场的汽油供应减少约五分之一，汽油出口则增长59%，从8月每日973万升增至9月每日1547万升。该炼油厂还向自有库存增加每日325万升，9月底汽油库存达到3.662亿升，而8月底为3.604亿升。

汽油进口量下降引发了供应中断的担忧，尤其是年末通常需求会增加。在汽油库存覆盖天数连续7个月低于30天基准的情况下，分析师担心，随着节日季临近，供应进一步下降可能引发国内短缺。然而，尼日利亚大型能源经销商协会（MEMAN）秘书Clement Isong并未立即就协会成员进口量骤降给出具体解释。他回应LEADERSHIP的询问时说：“让我核实一下并查明情况。不过，我正努力从更广泛的角度看待你们的担忧，并作出恰当分析。”

一名同样从事石油产品进口的行业消息人士则告诉LEADERSHIP，一些金融机构拒绝向石油产品经销商签发信用证。该消息人士无法证实所谓拒发的原因，但另一名行业消息人士声称，银行正受到压力或胁迫，无法向进口商提供信贷支持。

私营企业促进中心（CPPE）首席执行官Muda Yusuf博士给出了另一种解释，认为进口下降可能与原油价格上涨有关，目前原油价格约为每桶115美元。Yusuf说：“我认为，这完全取决于商业决策，也与金融机构不愿承担损失风险有关。”他解释道，企业和金融机构必须考虑向价格波动的大宗商品投入资金所带来的风险。Yusuf还警告称，美国与俄罗斯之间持续进行的谈判可能引发原油价格突然下跌；如果进口商以较高价格购入产品，届时可能遭受巨额损失。

与此同时，尼日利亚石油产品零售站业主协会（PETROAN）全国主席Billy Gillis-Harry王子博士淡化了人们对可能短缺的担忧，称NMDPRA已采取措施保障供应。他对LEADERSHIP表示，监管机构掌握监测供应所需的全部数据，并将确保通过进口或国内采购弥补任何供应缺口。

去年数据表明，汽油需求在年末可能大幅上升，从而进一步加大当前库存水平面临的压力。以卡车运出量衡量，汽油消费量从2025年9月每日4380万升增至10月每日5670万升，并在12月达到每日6370万升的峰值。2026年9月消费量为每日4440万升。因此，若需求恢复到2025年12月的水平，增幅约为43%。

去年，在供应增加后，汽油库存覆盖天数在12月恢复至29.3天，并在1月达到33天。11月和12月每日接收量分别达到7150万升和7420万升，其中进口量分别为每日5210万升和4220万升。

根据9月的库存覆盖天数和消费量估算，当前汽油库存约为10.6亿升。按照2025年12月每日6370万升的消费速度计算，这一库存量约可维持16.7天。若要在这一消费水平下维持30天的库存覆盖天数，约需19亿升汽油。任何额外进口货物都将按照当时的市场基准定价。9月，评估基准的Brent原油价格为每桶116.77美元，奈拉兑美元汇率为N1,327.31。各加油站指导价从拉各斯每升N1,371.01至迈杜古里每升N1,464.75不等。

家用燃气，也就是液化石油气（LPG）的供应状况比汽油更为紧张，库存覆盖天数仍显著低于监管基准。9月LPG库存覆盖天数为15.9天，比门槛低14.1天，据报消费量达到基准的133.3%。LPG每日接收量增长9%至4.7千吨，主要得益于国内供应增长50%至4.5千吨。不过，进口量下降85%至0.2千吨。国内来源约占LPG接收量的96%，消费量则增长8%，升至每日5.2千吨。

相比之下，柴油和航空燃料的库存水平保持在安全门槛以上。柴油库存覆盖天数为49.7天，航空燃料库存覆盖天数为53.2天。尽管库存相对充足，柴油每日接收量仍下降40%，从8月的1450万升降至9月的870万升，创监管机构数据所覆盖13个月中的最低水平。国内柴油接收量下降39%，从每日1320万升降至每日810万升；进口量下降54%，从每日130万升降至每日60万升。不过，消费量略升，从每日1430万升增至每日145万升。Dangote的柴油产量增长35%，达到每日2432万升。但其国内交付量从每日1237万升降至每日814万升，出口量则增长82%，从每日875万升升至每日1591万升。该炼油厂9月底柴油库存为2.325亿升，而8月底为1.372亿升。

1. 库存覆盖天数仍低于安全水平。9月汽油库存覆盖天数为23.9天，比30天基准少6.1天，已连续7个月低于该水平。5月曾降至16.2天的低点，此后逐月回升，但回升速度正在放缓。

2. 进口量正在下降。9月汽油进口量下降30%，从每日1460万升降至每日1020万升，原因是获批进口许可证对应的进口量已经用尽。总接收量下降23%至每日3870万升，消费量则增长7%至每日4440万升。

3. Dangote产量增加，但本地交付量减少。该炼油厂产量增长13%，达到每日4722万升，但面向国内市场的汽油供应减少约五分之一。汽油出口飙升59%，达到每日1547万升，同时增加了自有库存。

4. 经销商削减进口的原因尚有争议。一名行业消息人士称，银行拒绝向进口商签发信用证。另一人则称银行正受到压力而这样做。这些原因尚未得到证实，MEMAN秘书Clement Isong也没有解释进口下降的原因。CPPE的Muda Yusuf博士称，这是一项商业决策：原油价格约为每桶115美元。

5. 节日季才是真正的风险。去年，汽油消费量从9月每日4380万升增至12月每日6370万升。若这一趋势重演，需求将增加约43%。按这一速度计算，当前约10.61亿升的库存仅能维持约16.7天。若要保持30天的库存覆盖天数，则需要约19亿升。

https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/26/d.title: Despite Cut in MPR, Average Maximum Lending Rate Rises to 32.62%
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/26/d.summary: Despite the reduction of the Monetary Policy Rate (MPR) to 23 per cent by the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) of the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) in its last meeting, the banking sector’s average maximum lending rate increased to 32.62 per cent in September 2026 from 29.20 per cent in August 2026. Maximum lending rate refers to the highest permissible interest rate that lenders can charge borrowers.
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/26/d.summary_zh: 尽管尼日利亚中央银行（CBN）货币政策委员会（MPC）在上次会议上将货币政策利率（MPR）下调至23%，但银行业平均最高贷款利率仍从2026年8月的29.20%升至2026年9月的32.62%。最高贷款利率是指贷款机构可向借款人收取的最高法定利率。
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/26/d.body: Despite the reduction of the Monetary Policy Rate (MPR) to 23 per cent by the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) of the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) in its last meeting, the banking sector’s average maximum lending rate increased to 32.62 per cent in September 2026 from 29.20 per cent in August 2026. Maximum lending rate refers to the highest permissible interest rate that lenders can charge borrowers. The rate is crucial for ensuring fair lending practices and protecting borrowers from excessive interest rates. According to the CBN Money Market Indicators, the average maximum lending had opened January 2026 at 32.68 per cent when MPR was at 27 per cent, and reached a peak of 35.17 per cent in March 2026 as MPR stood at 26.50 per cent. An investigation by THISDAY revealed that most Nigerian banks’ maximum lending rate remained flat between September and October 9, 2026 amid the 350 basis points MPR cut by MPC. Specifically, between September 4, 2026 and October 9, 2026, “Manufacturing sector” maximum lending rates of Access Bank, Alpha Morgan Merchant Bank, Coronation Merchant Bank and Ecobank remained flat at 32.28 per cent, 35.00 per cent, and 35 per cent respectively. In the period under review, Citi Bank saw its Manufacturing sector maximum lending rate drop to 19 per cent from 20 per cent, while Quest Merchant Bank Manufacturing sector maximum lending rate moved to 30 per cent from 35 per cent. In June 2026, the International Monetary Fund (IMF) had expressed that Nigerian banks are quick to raise lending rates when the CBN tightens monetary policy, but slow to reduce borrowing costs when rates are eased. The Washington-based institution said the country’s monetary policy transmission mechanism has strengthened since the unification of the foreign exchange (FX) market in June 2023, although distortions within the banking system still persist. According to the IMF, interest rate transmission in Nigeria follows what economists describe as a ‘rockets-and-feathers’ pattern, where banks rapidly increase lending rates during tightening cycles but are reluctant to reduce them when policy conditions soften. The report stated that a 100 basis-point increase in the MPR typically pushes treasury bill and lending rates up by about 175 to 180 basis points almost immediately. However, a similar rate cut results in only a 25 to 30 basis-point decline in borrowing costs. “This asymmetry — statistically significant — implies that banks transmit tightening rapidly and even amplify it but adjust much more slowly during easing cycles,” the IMF said. The institution noted that interbank rates respond more evenly to both tightening and easing, while deposit rates remain largely unresponsive in either direction. The IMF attributed the weak response in deposit rates to limited competition among banks for customer deposits and the existence of what it described as ‘captive depositors’ with limited investment alternatives. CBN data revealed that the average prime lending rate also rose to .19.04 per cent in September 2026 from 17.86per cent in August 2026. In January 2026, the average prime lending rate was at 19.54 per cent, making it the highest so far since 2006. The prime lending rate indicates the possible rate offered to the most creditworthy customers by Nigerian banks. Nigeria’s average prime lending rate reached an all-time high of 19.66 per cent in November 2009 and a record low of 11.13per cent in March 2021. The steady increase in interest rate reflected in the average prime lending rate last year as the CBN intensified its effort to tackle inflation rate and stabilize the local currency at the foreign exchange market. Reacting, Investment Banker & Stockbroker, Tajudeen Olayinka stated that Nigerian banks are not compelling to adjusted lending rate to MPR, but to use it as a guide to pricing and repricing loans and advances, plus other financial instruments, in a manner that gives credence to risk/return framework associated with different loan applicants. “You’ll recall MPR was adjusted to 23per cent, to make it aligned with what the market is asking for. Only prime borrowers will receive an interest rate that is close to MPR or risk-free rate. It is also a function of demand and supply,” he said. Also, the Vice President, Highcap Securities, David Adonri stated that the increase in lending rate in the Nigerian banking sector means there was tight money supply in the credit market in September 2026 despite massive cuts in MPR. Cordros Research in a report stated that it expected the market performance to be shaped by the extent to which the policy adjustment translates into lower market yields, improved liquidity and reduced corporate financing costs. “Continued macroeconomic stability, particularly in inflation and the exchange rate, will also remain important to investor sentiment. Against this backdrop, 2026FY earnings and dividend announcements, foreign and domestic portfolio flows, corporate actions and company-specific developments are likely to be the key drivers of the market performance in Q4-2026,” the firm had explained. However, analysts have predicted a further increase in the average maximum lending and primer lending rate amid steady ease in inflation figures. https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/26/d.title_zh: 尽管平均优惠利率下调，平均最高贷款利率却升至32.62%
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/26/d.body_zh: 尽管尼日利亚中央银行（CBN）货币政策委员会（MPC）在上次会议上将货币政策利率（MPR）下调至23%，但银行业平均最高贷款利率却从2026年8月的29.20%升至2026年9月的32.62%。最高贷款利率是指贷款机构可向借款人收取的最高法定利率。这一利率对于确保公平放贷、保护借款人免受过高利息负担至关重要。根据CBN货币市场指标，2026年1月MPR为27%时，平均最高贷款利率期初为32.68%；2026年3月MPR维持在26.50%时，该利率达到35.17%的峰值。THISDAY的一项调查显示，在MPC将MPR下调350个基点的情况下，多数尼日利亚银行的最高贷款利率在2026年9月至10月9日期间保持不变。具体而言，2026年9月4日至10月9日期间，Access Bank、Alpha Morgan Merchant Bank、Coronation Merchant Bank和Ecobank的“制造业”最高贷款利率分别维持在32.28%、35.00%和35%。在考察期内，Citi Bank的“制造业”最高贷款利率从20%降至19%，Quest Merchant Bank的“制造业”最高贷款利率则从35%降至30%。2026年6月，国际货币基金组织（IMF）曾表示，当CBN收紧货币政策时，尼日利亚银行会迅速提高贷款利率，但在宽松政策降低利率时，却迟迟不愿下调借款成本。这家总部位于华盛顿的机构表示，自2023年6月外汇市场统一以来，尼日利亚货币政策传导机制有所增强，但银行体系内部仍存在扭曲。IMF称，尼日利亚的利率传导呈现经济学家所谓的“火箭与羽毛”模式，即银行在紧缩周期内迅速上调贷款利率，但在政策条件宽松时却不愿降低利率。报告指出，MPR每上调100个基点，通常会立即推动国库券和贷款利率上升约175至180个基点；然而，幅度相近的降息只会使借款成本下降25至30个基点。IMF表示：“这种不对称性在统计上显著，说明银行会迅速传导紧缩政策，甚至放大紧缩效果，但在宽松周期内调整速度要慢得多。”该机构指出，银行间利率对紧缩和宽松政策的反应较为均衡，而存款利率无论政策向哪个方向调整，基本都缺乏明显反应。IMF将存款利率反应迟缓归因于银行争夺客户存款的竞争有限，以及存在其所称的“被俘获储户”，这些储户可选择的投资替代品十分有限。CBN数据显示，平均最优惠贷款利率也从2026年8月的17.86%升至2026年9月的19.04%。2026年1月，平均最优惠贷款利率为19.54%，成为2006年以来的最高水平。最优惠贷款利率反映尼日利亚银行可能向信用状况最佳客户提供的利率。尼日利亚平均最优惠贷款利率曾于2009年11月创下19.66%的历史最高水平，并于2021年3月降至11.13%的历史最低水平。去年，随着CBN加大抗击通胀、稳定本币在外汇市场汇率的力度，平均最优惠贷款利率所反映的利率持续上升。对此，Investment Banker & Stockbroker的Tajudeen Olayinka表示，尼日利亚银行并未被要求将贷款利率与MPR调整保持一致，而是须将MPR作为贷款、预付款及其他金融工具定价和重新定价的参考，使定价符合不同借款申请人的风险与收益框架。他说：“请记得，MPR已调整为23%，目的是使其与市场需求相匹配。只有优质借款人才能获得接近MPR或无风险利率的利率。这同样取决于供求关系。”Highcap Securities副总裁David Adonri也表示，尽管MPR大幅下调，但2026年9月尼日利亚银行业贷款利率上升，意味着信贷市场资金供应紧张。Cordros Research在一份报告中表示，预计市场表现将取决于政策调整在多大程度上转化为市场收益率下降、流动性改善和企业融资成本下降。该公司解释道：“持续的宏观稳定，尤其是通胀和汇率稳定，仍将对投资者情绪至关重要。在此背景下，2026财年的盈利和股息公告、境内外投资组合资金流动、公司行动及公司特定发展，可能成为推动2026年第四季度市场表现的关键因素。”不过，分析师预测，随着通胀数据持续回落，平均最高贷款利率和最优惠贷款利率还将进一步上升。THISDAY成立于1995年1月22日，由THISDAY https://leadership.ng/akwa-ibom-pledges-.title: Akwa Ibom Pledges More Support For Vulnerable Residents
https://leadership.ng/akwa-ibom-pledges-.summary: According to her, the interventions cover food security, support for vulnerable households, housing for disadvantaged families, women and youth empowerment, assistance for elderly citizens, inclusion of persons with disabilities, and emergency and disaster response. She said the creation of a dedicated Ministry of Humanitarian Affairs reflected the governor’s commitment to coordinating interventions, strengthening social protection and ensuring vulnerable individuals and families received organised support.
https://leadership.ng/akwa-ibom-pledges-.summary_zh: 据她介绍，这些干预措施涵盖粮食安全、为弱势家庭提供支持、为处境不利的家庭提供住房、赋权妇女和青年、为老年公民提供帮助、确保残障人士获得包容，以及开展紧急和灾害应对工作。她说，设立专门的人道主义事务部体现了州长承诺协调各项干预措施、强化社会保护，并确保弱势个人和家庭获得有组织的支持。
https://leadership.ng/akwa-ibom-pledges-.body: The Commissioner for Humanitarian Affairs, Princess Emem Ibanga, gave the assurance at the weekend during the launch of the EL ZAIN Women, Children and Peace Development Initiative at IBOM LED, along IBB Avenue, Uyo. Ibanga described the administration’s policies as people-centred, noting that the government had invested billions of naira in welfare interventions over the past three years. She said the humanitarian governance model was designed to integrate vulnerable and disadvantaged people into the government’s programmes and address their needs. According to her, the interventions cover food security, support for vulnerable households, housing for disadvantaged families, women and youth empowerment, assistance for elderly citizens, inclusion of persons with disabilities, and emergency and disaster response. She said the creation of a dedicated Ministry of Humanitarian Affairs reflected the governor’s commitment to coordinating interventions, strengthening social protection and ensuring vulnerable individuals and families received organised support. The commissioner commended the EL ZAIN initiative for its humanitarian work and urged its leadership to sustain its partnership with the ministry and align its programmes with the state’s priorities. “I am pleased that the EL ZAIN Women, Children and Peace Development Initiative has registered with the ministry. I encourage its leadership to sustain this relationship and align its programmes with the state’s humanitarian priorities and coordination framework,” she said. Chairman of the launch, Paul Usoro, SAN, praised the support provided by the founder’s husband, describing it as a demonstration of the initiative’s slogan, “love in action”. Usoro called for prayers and material support for the initiative, saying humanitarian service required collective effort. The founder, Dr Zeinab Akpan, described the launch as a new beginning in humanitarian assistance, recalling that the initiative grew out of years of engaging with disadvantaged people, supporting vulnerable households and offering guidance to those in need. She said her experience as Acting President of the Naval Officers’ Wives Association (NOWA) strengthened her resolve to develop structured programmes to support vulnerable groups. According to her, the initiative would focus on empowering women, nurturing children, promoting peace, encouraging self-reliance, and supporting education and dialogue. She said the initiative was associated with the Institute of Public Policy and Diplomacy Research (IPPDR), New York, and aligned with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals on gender equality, education and peace. Akpan listed the initiative’s planned interventions to include micro-business grants for 20 women selected through a screening process, healthcare support, assistance with hospital bills, educational awards for students who finish first to third in their categories, and childcare support across local government areas. She thanked Governor Eno and the commissioner for their support, urging stakeholders to take practical steps to improve the lives of vulnerable people. The initiative’s Executive Director, Rear Admiral Joseph Akpan (retd.), said his wife’s difficult childhood experiences inspired the establishment of the foundation. He expressed gratitude that the initiative was beginning to yield results and pledged to expand its work through partnerships with other organisations. We’ve got the edge. https://leadership.ng/akwa-ibom-pledges-.title_zh: 阿夸伊博姆承诺为弱势居民提供更多支持
https://leadership.ng/akwa-ibom-pledges-.body_zh: 人道事务专员埃梅姆·伊班加公主于周末在位于乌约IBB大道沿线IBOM LED举行的“EL ZAIN妇女、儿童与和平发展倡议”启动仪式上作出上述保证。伊班加称本届政府的政策以人为本，并指出，过去三年政府已投入数十亿奈拉用于福利干预。她说，人道治理模式旨在将弱势和处境不利群体纳入政府各项计划，满足他们的需求。据她介绍，这些干预措施涵盖粮食安全、为弱势家庭提供支持、为处境不利家庭提供住房、赋权妇女和青年、援助老年公民、吸纳残障人士，以及开展紧急救援和灾害应对。她说，设立专门的人道事务部体现了州长对协调各项干预措施、加强社会保护以及确保弱势个人和家庭获得有组织支持的承诺。专员称赞EL ZAIN倡议的人道工作，并敦促其领导层维持与该部的合作关系，使各项计划与本州优先事项相衔接。她说：“我很高兴EL ZAIN妇女、儿童与和平发展倡议已在本部登记注册。我鼓励其领导层维持这层关系，并使各项计划与本州的人道优先事项和协调框架相衔接。”启动仪式主席保罗·乌索罗律师称赞了创办人的丈夫所提供的支持，称这是该倡议“行动中的爱”这一口号的体现。乌索罗呼吁为该倡议祈祷并提供物质支持，称人道服务需要集体努力。创办人泽纳布·阿克潘博士称，此次启动标志着人道援助的新起点，并回顾称，该倡议源于她多年来与处境不利群体接触、扶持弱势家庭以及为有需要者提供指导的历程。她说，担任海军军官夫人协会（NOWA）代理主席的经历，强化了她制定结构化计划以支持弱势群体的决心。据她介绍，该倡议将重点关注赋权妇女、关怀儿童、促进和平、鼓励自立，以及支持教育和对话。她说，该倡议与纽约公共政策与外交研究所（IPPDR）合作，并与联合国关于性别平等、教育与和平的可持续发展目标相契合。阿克潘列出的计划干预措施包括：通过筛选程序选出的20名女性获得微型企业补助、医疗支持、医院账单援助，为各自类别中名列第一至第三的学生颁发教育奖励，以及在地方政府辖区提供儿童照护支持。她感谢州长埃诺和专员的支持，敦促各方采取切实行动，改善弱势群体的生活。该倡议执行主任约瑟夫·阿克潘海军少校（退役）表示，妻子艰难坎坷的童年经历促使她创立该基金会。他对倡议开始取得成果表示感激，并承诺通过与其他组织建立合作来扩大工作。我们掌握独家优势。实时报道、独家内幕和独家视角将直接发送到您的手机。不要满足于陈旧新闻。加入LEADERSHIP NEWS，通过WhatsApp获取全天候最新消息 →

https://prnigeria.com/2026/10/25/nigeria.title: Nigeria Customs Tests New Cargo Scanners, Tracking Systems in China
https://prnigeria.com/2026/10/25/nigeria.summary: The Nigeria Customs Service (NCS) and Trade Modernisation Project Limited (TMPL) have completed factory acceptance tests for newly acquired cargo scanners and electronic tracking systems in China ahead of their deployment in Nigeria. The new scanners are designed to examine cargo without requiring routine physical opening of containers, while the electronic tracking system will enable Customs officers to monitor consignments in real time as they move from ports to their final destinations.
https://prnigeria.com/2026/10/25/nigeria.summary_zh: 尼日利亚海关总署（NCS）与贸易现代化项目有限公司（TMPL）在中国完成了新购置货物扫描仪和电子追踪系统的工厂验收测试，随后这些设备将部署到尼日利亚。新扫描仪能够在无需例行打开集装箱的情况下检查货物，电子追踪系统则将使海关官员能够实时监控货物从港口运往最终目的地的全过程。
https://prnigeria.com/2026/10/25/nigeria.body: The Nigeria Customs Service (NCS) and Trade Modernisation Project Limited (TMPL) have completed factory acceptance tests for newly acquired cargo scanners and electronic tracking systems in China ahead of their deployment in Nigeria. The equipment is expected to strengthen cargo examination, improve revenue collection, curb cargo diversion and enhance the detection of concealed and prohibited items at the country’s entry and exit points. The two-week Factory Acceptance Test (FAT), conducted from October 9 to 20, 2026, took place at the facilities of Nuctech Company Limited, the Chinese manufacturer of the equipment. The exercise was led by the Deputy Comptroller-General of Customs in charge of the Information Communication and Technology/Modernisation Department, Oluyomi Adebakin, and involved technical experts from the NCS and TMPL. The team conducted technical verification of the newly acquired Non-Intrusive Inspection (NII) equipment and Electronic Cargo Tracking System (ECTS) to ensure they met contractual specifications and international operational standards before shipment to Nigeria. Speaking during the exercise, Adebakin reaffirmed Comptroller-General of Customs Adewale Adeniyi’s commitment to deploying modern technology to facilitate legitimate trade, optimise revenue generation and strengthen national security. She described the factory acceptance test as a critical quality-assurance process that would ensure the equipment was fit for purpose before deployment. The new scanners are designed to examine cargo without requiring routine physical opening of containers, while the electronic tracking system will enable Customs officers to monitor consignments in real time as they move from ports to their final destinations. The integration of both technologies is expected to improve cargo visibility, strengthen risk management and reduce opportunities for diversion and other irregularities along the supply chain. Also speaking, the Acting Comptroller of Non-Intrusive Inspection, Deputy Comptroller of Customs Umar Madugu, said the deployment of the equipment would significantly reduce the need for 100 per cent physical examination of cargo. According to him, the systems would minimise human contact in cargo inspection, curb diversion and improve operational efficiency across Customs formations. Madugu added that the technology would support more targeted inspections, allowing officers to concentrate on high-risk consignments while facilitating faster clearance for compliant traders. Speaking on behalf of TMPL, the company’s General Manager, Bamidele Chinedu, described the factory acceptance test as a significant milestone in the implementation of the Trade Modernisation Project. He said the integration of NII scanners and the Electronic Cargo Tracking System was central to establishing a transparent, efficient and technology-driven Customs administration. Chinedu noted that combining modern scanning technology with electronic cargo monitoring would strengthen operational controls and support the Service’s broader modernisation agenda. In his remarks, Niu Chao, Project Manager at Nuctech Company Limited, expressed the company’s commitment to delivering world-class equipment and providing the technical support required for effective implementation. He also assured the Nigerian delegation of continued assistance through capacity building, equipment maintenance and after-sales services to support the systems’ long-term performance. Beyond the equipment verification, technical experts from the NCS and TMPL received training during the exercise on the operation, handling and maintenance of the scanners and electronic tracking systems. The training is expected to equip Nigerian personnel with the technical skills required for the equipment’s deployment, routine operation and maintenance, while reducing potential disruptions after installation. The factory acceptance test marks a key stage in preparations for introducing the new technology into Nigeria’s Customs operations. Once deployed, the systems are expected to support faster cargo processing, improve compliance monitoring, strengthen revenue assurance and enhance the Service’s capacity to detect illicit goods. The initiative forms part of the NCS’s broader modernisation drive to use digital technology and automation to improve trade facilitation, operational transparency and border security
https://prnigeria.com/2026/10/25/nigeria.title_zh: 尼日利亚海关在中国测试新货物扫描仪和追踪系统
https://prnigeria.com/2026/10/25/nigeria.body_zh: 尼日利亚海关总署（NCS）和贸易现代化项目有限公司（TMPL）在中国对新购置的货物扫描仪和电子追踪系统完成了出厂验收测试，随后这些设备将部署到尼日利亚。这些设备有望加强货物查验、提高税收征管效率、遏制货物转移，并增强该国口岸发现藏匿物品和违禁品的能力。此次为期两周的出厂验收测试（FAT）于2026年10月9日至20日进行，地点是设备中国制造商Nuctech Company Limited的厂区。测试由负责信息通信技术及现代化部门的海关副总监长Oluyomi Adebakin主持，尼日利亚海关总署和TMPL的技术专家参与。测试团队对新购置的非侵入式检查（NII）设备和电子货物追踪系统（ECTS）进行了技术核验，以确保其符合合同规格和国际运行标准后再运往尼日利亚。Adebakin在测试期间表示，海关总监长Adewale Adeniyi重申了部署现代技术的决心，以促进合法贸易、优化收入增长并加强国家安全。她称，出厂验收测试是一项关键的质量保证流程，可确保设备在部署前适合其预期用途。新扫描仪能够在无需例行拆开集装箱的情况下检查货物，电子追踪系统则将使海关官员能够实时监控货物从港口运往最终目的地的全过程。两项技术的整合有望提高货物可视性、强化风险管理，并减少供应链中出现货物转移及其他违规行为的机会。代理非侵入式检查总监长、海关副总监长Umar Madugu也表示，部署这些设备将显著减少对货物进行100%人工实物查验的需要。他说，这些系统将尽量减少货物查验中的人为接触，遏制货物转移，并提高海关各部门的运行效率。Madugu补充称，这项技术将支持更有针对性的查验，使官员能够集中处理高风险货物，同时为合规贸易商提供更快捷的通关服务。TMPL总经理Bamidele Chinedu代表公司发言时，将此次出厂验收测试描述为贸易现代化项目实施过程中的一个重要里程碑。他说，整合非侵入式检查扫描仪与电子货物追踪系统，是建立透明、高效且以技术驱动的海关管理体系的核心。Chinedu指出，将现代扫描技术与电子货物监控相结合，将强化运营管控，并支持海关总署更广泛的现代化议程。Nuctech Company Limited项目经理Niu Chao在发言中表示，该公司致力于提供世界一流的设备，并为设备的有效实施提供所需的技术支持。他还承诺，通过能力建设、设备维护和售后服务，继续向尼日利亚代表团提供协助，以支持这些系统的长期运行。除核验设备外，尼日利亚海关总署和TMPL的技术专家还在此次活动中接受了有关扫描仪和电子追踪系统操作、使用与维护的培训。此次培训将使尼日利亚人员掌握设备部署、日常运行和维护所需的技术技能，同时降低安装后可能出现的运行中断。出厂验收测试标志着将该新技术引入尼日利亚海关业务准备工作的一个关键阶段。系统部署后，有望加快货物处理、改善合规监管、强化税收保障，并增强海关总署发现非法商品的能力。该举措是尼日利亚海关总署更广泛现代化计划的一部分，旨在利用数字技术和自动化手段促进贸易便利化、提高运营透明度并加强边境安全

https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/opinion/edi.title: Kim's China visit must lead to restraint
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/opinion/edi.summary: North Korean leader Kim Jong-un’s surprise visit to China is a reminder that the Korean Peninsula’s future cannot be understood through inter-Korean relations alone. For South Korea, the appropriate response is neither alarmism nor wishful thinking, but rather a clear-eyed assessment of what closer ties between China and North Korea could mean for regional security, sanctions enforcement and diplomacy. The visit carried both historical symbolism and practical economic significance.
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/opinion/edi.summary_zh: 朝鲜领导人金正恩突然访问中国，提醒人们仅凭韩朝关系无法理解朝鲜半岛的未来。对韩国而言，适当的回应既不是危言耸听，也不是一厢情愿，而是清醒评估中朝关系加深将如何影响地区安全、制裁执行和外交。此次访问兼具历史象征意义和实际经济意义。
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/opinion/edi.body: North Korean leader Kim Jong-un’s surprise visit to China is a reminder that the Korean Peninsula’s future cannot be understood through inter-Korean relations alone. Kim's crossing into Dandong via the newly opened New Amnok River Bridge and his meetings with senior Chinese official Wang Huning underscore the strategic importance Pyongyang attaches to Beijing. For South Korea, the appropriate response is neither alarmism nor wishful thinking, but rather a clear-eyed assessment of what closer ties between China and North Korea could mean for regional security, sanctions enforcement and diplomacy. The visit carried both historical symbolism and practical economic significance. Kim paid tribute to China’s participation in the Korean War and toured an automobile factory with Wang, who conveyed greetings from Chinese President Xi Jinping. The itinerary highlighted a relationship grounded in shared history but increasingly shaped by material interests. Notably, however, Kim did not meet Xi. The visit should therefore be judged on what it demonstrably achieved, not inflated into evidence of a diplomatic breakthrough that has yet to materialize. The new bridge merits particular scrutiny. Better transport links can facilitate legitimate trade, sustain livelihoods and ease North Korea’s isolation. Economic engagement is not inherently inimical to peace. Its implications, however, depend on what crosses the border and whether transactions are properly monitored. Beijing must ensure that deeper economic cooperation remains consistent with its international obligations and does not create new channels for prohibited transfers that could advance Pyongyang’s weapons programs. China cannot credibly champion regional stability while treating North Korea’s military provocations as a problem for others to manage. Its renewed access to Kim’s leadership presents an opportunity to discourage escalation, encourage communication and reinforce the costs of confrontation. Beijing need not sever ties with Pyongyang to exercise such influence. On the contrary, it should recognize that an increasingly volatile peninsula threatens the economic and strategic interests that closer bilateral relations are meant to serve. Kim, too, should recognize the limits of a foreign policy built around powerful patrons. Stronger relations with China and Russia may expand his diplomatic options and provide economic or strategic support, but they cannot deliver lasting security or broad-based prosperity on their own. A strategy that seeks external assistance while excluding South Korea from meaningful dialogue would only entrench the peninsula’s division. Sustainable economic development requires predictability, and predictability is impossible when the risk of military conflict remains high. Seoul must respond with equal resolve and strategic discipline. Robust deterrence and close coordination with Washington remain indispensable. But deterrence should create space for diplomacy, not become a substitute for it. South Korea should maintain active channels with Beijing, pursue practical cooperation on crisis prevention and assess closer China-North Korea ties by their actual consequences. A measurable reduction in military threats would be welcome. Any use of enhanced cooperation to embolden coercion would require a firm and coordinated response. Nor should Seoul define diplomatic progress solely by whether Kim meets U.S. President Donald Trump again. Speculation about another summit should not be mistaken for a confirmed diplomatic process. A hastily arranged encounter could produce striking images and short-lived optimism without yielding durable commitments. Any renewed negotiations must include close consultation with Seoul and focus on concrete, verifiable measures to reduce nuclear dangers and prevent miscalculation. The immediate priority should be to restore military communication, prevent incidents along the border and preserve avenues for humanitarian engagement. Such steps would not resolve the nuclear question, but they could address one of the peninsula’s most dangerous vulnerabilities: the absence of reliable mechanisms for managing confrontation. Seoul should advance these proposals without assuming that Pyongyang will accept them readily. An offer of dialogue is a strategic choice, not a guarantee of reciprocity. Kim’s journey across the Amnok River demonstrates that North Korea will open doors when its leadership sees an advantage. The challenge is to turn selective engagement into a broader contribution to regional security. Beijing should use its influence responsibly, Pyongyang should reconsider the costs of sustained hostility and Seoul should pair credible deterrence with sustained diplomatic initiative. A bridge can connect two banks; only prudent policy can make it a passage toward peace
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/opinion/edi.title_zh: 金正恩访华必须带来克制
https://www.koreatimes.co.kr/opinion/edi.body_zh: 朝鲜领导人金正恩突然访问中国，再次表明，仅凭韩朝关系无法理解朝鲜半岛的未来。金正恩经新通车的鸭绿江大桥进入丹东，并会见中国高级官员王沪宁，凸显平壤赋予北京的重要战略意义。对韩国而言，适当的回应既不是危言耸听，也不是一厢情愿，而是清醒评估中朝关系走近可能给地区安全、制裁执行和外交带来何种影响。此次访问既具有历史象征意义，也具有实际经济意义。金正恩向中国参加朝鲜战争一事致敬，并与王沪宁一同参观汽车工厂；王沪宁转达了中国国家主席习近平的问候。访问日程凸显了两国关系建立在共同历史之上，但正日益受到现实利益影响。然而，金正恩此次并未与习近平会面。因此，应根据此次访问切实取得的成果来评价它，而不应将其夸大为迄今尚未实现的外交突破。新桥尤其值得审视。更便利的交通连接能够促进合法贸易、维持民生并缓解朝鲜的孤立。经济接触本身并不必然与和平相悖。然而，其影响取决于跨境流通的是什么，以及相关交易是否得到妥善监督。北京必须确保，更深入的经济合作符合其国际义务，不会为被禁止的转让行为开辟新渠道，从而推动平壤的武器计划。中国不能一面标榜维护地区稳定，一面把朝鲜的军事挑衅当成应由他人处理的问题。重新接触金正恩领导层，为中国创造了劝阻局势升级、鼓励沟通并强化对抗代价的机会。北京无须切断与平壤的关系，便能发挥这种影响。相反，中国应当认识到，日益动荡的朝鲜半岛会威胁更密切的双边关系本应服务的经济和战略利益。金正恩也应认识到，围绕强大靠山构建外交政策的局限。改善与中国和俄罗斯的关系或许能扩大他的外交选择，并提供经济或战略支持，但这些关系本身无法带来持久安全或广泛繁荣。寻求外部援助、却将韩国排除在实质性对话之外的战略，只会进一步固化半岛分裂。可持续经济发展需要可预测性，而军事冲突风险依然高企时，可预测性便无从谈起。首尔必须以同等决心和战略纪律作出回应。有效的威慑以及与华盛顿密切协调仍不可或缺。但威慑应当为外交创造空间，而不是取代外交。韩国应保持与北京的活跃沟通渠道，就危机预防开展务实合作，并根据中朝关系走近的实际后果加以评估。若军事威胁得到可量化减少，将是值得欢迎的成果。任何利用加强后的合作来助长胁迫的行为，都将需要坚决且协调一致的回应。首尔也不应仅以金正恩是否再次会见美国总统唐纳德·特朗普来界定外交进展。关于再次举行峰会的猜测，不应被误认为已确认的外交进程。仓促安排会晤可能制造醒目的画面和短暂的乐观情绪，却不会产生持久承诺。任何重启的谈判都必须包括与首尔的密切磋商，并聚焦于降低核危险和防止误判的具体、可核查措施。眼下的优先事项应是恢复军事沟通、防止边境发生意外事件，以及为人道主义接触保留渠道。这些举措无法解决核问题，但可以处理半岛上最危险的脆弱性之一：缺乏管理对抗局势的可靠机制。首尔应推动这些提议，同时不假定平壤会欣然接受。提出对话是一项战略选择，并不保证对方会予以回应。金正恩跨越鸭绿江的行程表明，当朝鲜领导层看到有利条件时，朝鲜愿意打开大门。挑战在于把有选择的接触转化为对地区安全的更广泛贡献。北京应负责任地运用影响力，平壤应重新审视持续敌对的代价，首尔则应把可信的威慑与持续的外交倡议结合起来。桥梁能够连接两岸；只有审慎的政策才能使其成为通往和平的通道

https://www.rappler.com/world/us-canada/.body: Already have Rappler+? Sign in to listen to groundbreaking journalism. A man holds a 'Vote Blue' sign while sitting in a golf cart during a Democratic rally in The Villages, Florida, US, October 17, 2026. WASHINGTON, USA – Nonpartisan analysts say Democrats stand a good chance of winning the US House of Representatives and possibly the Senate in the November 3 midterm elections , which would give them a slice of power in Washington after two years of Republican control. Democrats argue that Republicans have allowed President Donald Trump ‘s administration to declare war and control spending, even though the US Constitution reserves those powers for lawmakers. Here are some ways a Democratic Congress could hem in Trump’s foreign policy. Trump did not secure approval from Congress before he launched the war with Iran on February 28 , and Democrats have voted repeatedly to end the fighting unless he does so. One of these resolutions passed with support from a handful of Republicans, but Trump’s administration ignored it. With control of the House or the Senate, Democrats could cut defense spending to pressure Trump to obtain permission from Congress to continue the war. They could also require administration officials to testify publicly about their plans. Trump has largely halted direct US financial and military aid to Ukraine, despite broad support from Democratic and Republican lawmakers as it fights a Russian invasion . Most recently, he has angered members of Congress, including many Republicans, by lifting sanctions on Russian diesel and waiving sanctions on Russian energy only weeks after signing them into law. With a victory in both chambers in November, Democrats would be able to decide what gets voted on and when. That could allow them to approve new aid to Ukraine, which likely would pass with the two-thirds majorities needed to overcome a Trump veto. They could also target other Trump activities. For example, Representative Gregory Meeks of New York, who could head the House Foreign Affairs Committee if Democrats win control, has introduced bipartisan legislation to block Trump’s plan to bring Russian diesel back into the global market. Support for Israel has plummeted among Democrats over its conduct in the Gaza war, which has killed tens of thousands of Palestinian civilians. The ongoing violence in the Israeli-occupied West Bank and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s close alliance with Republicans have also been factors. Democrats could limit or end military aid to Israel, which amounted to $3.8 billion in the most recent fiscal year. That is more than was provided to any other country. Nearly half of House Democrats voted this summer to cut off aid to Israel. Some of those who voted against that effort, such as Meeks, have backed limits on providing weapons like heavy bombs to Israel. Democrats are far more likely than Trump’s Republicans to limit military spending. Trump asked for an unprecedented 67% increase in the military budget this year, to $1.5 trillion, but Democrats blocked it in the Senate, citing his refusal to consult Congress about the Iran war and his steep cuts to social programs. Trump has also withheld or canceled billions of dollars in foreign aid approved by Congress. Many Democrats have been angered by the cuts and say they will try to restore funding.
