https://leadership.ng/federal-government.body: “Gas has been a priority within that reform agenda because Nigeria is, as you all know, even more gas-rich than it is oil-rich, and the gas is arguably the most important physical resource for industrialisation,” special adviser to the President on Oil and Gas, Olu Verheijen said. According to her, government is now promoting gas production activities to secure firm energy security which will at the same create value in its industrialization efforts. Verheijen, disclosed this at the Africa Interviews Sustainability Forum 2026 in Lagos. She also said government has settled more than ₦100 billion in outstanding gas debts since January 2026, in a move aimed at strengthening the gas-to-power value chain and improving electricity supply. The payments were made under the Presidential Power Sector Financial Reform Programme and comes as Nigeria continues to grapple with electricity supply challenges, with gas supply and payments to producers remaining important to the performance of the power sector. Clearing outstanding obligations is expected to support confidence across the gas-to-power chain, although sustained improvement will also depend on regular payments, reliable gas delivery and the financial health of electricity market participants. Verheijen also highlighted government measures introduced since 2023 to encourage the use of liquefied petroleum gas, LPG, for household cooking. These include import duty waivers and zero-rated value-added tax measures for LPG and gas cylinders, intended to make cleaner cooking alternatives more accessible and reduce dependence on firewood. “A gas-rich nation cannot be comfortable while families remain stuck in the age of firewood,” she said. According to the presidential adviser, reforms under President Bola Tinubu’s administration are designed to remove barriers to investment and unlock Nigeria’s gas resources for industrialisation, electricity generation and economic growth. She disclosed that Nigeria had recorded four final investment decisions, FIDs, on gas projects in less than two years, while average daily gas production had increased from about seven billion cubic feet to eight billion cubic feet. Nigeria holds more than 200 trillion cubic feet of proven gas reserves, Verheijen said, but stressed that the country must attract sustained investment to convert its resource base into economic value. “A country can sit on enormous natural wealth and fail to turn it into energy to power industry, industries that create jobs and jobs that help us grow incomes,” she said. “What turns resources into prosperity is investment, consistent investment that responds to predictable incentives and a stable environment,” she added. Verheijen said Tinubu had directed his administration to identify and address the factors preventing investment from keeping pace with Nigeria’s economic potential. “When President Bola Tinubu assumed office in 2023, he gave us a very clear mandate: understand why investment has not moved at the pace of Nigeria’s potential and fix it,” she said. The four gas project investment decisions, including the Ima project in September 2026, reflect growing activity in the sector, Verheijen said. She also noted the increasing contribution of indigenous producers to domestic gas supply. Addressing Africa’s energy transition, she argued that governments across the continent should balance environmental sustainability with energy security, industrial development and job creation. “For Africa, the energy transition must mean transformation, molecules converted into megawatts, fertilizer, petrochemicals, cleaner mobility, manufacturing, jobs and exports,” she said. Verheijen also maintained that African countries should determine the pace of their energy transitions according to their development priorities and economic circumstances, rather than have those decisions imposed externally. “The energy transition must also mean agency. Africa is right to decide for itself how fast it decarbonises, rather than having those choices made for us by others. It is about affirming our right to be the authors of our own energy transition,” she said. She further emphasised the need to measure and reduce methane emissions from gas operations while ensuring that host communities benefit meaningfully from resource development. The settlement of the outstanding gas debts represents a step towards addressing financial constraints within Nigeria’s gas-to-power chain. However, the broader test will be whether improved payment discipline and investment translate into more reliable gas supplies, stronger electricity generation and better power delivery to homes and businesses. Meanwhile, Renaissance Africa Energy (RAE) says it’s growing its oil production to 500,000 barrels a day by 2030. The indigenous firm also said it will alongside this projection expand gas supply as part of broader efforts to improve Nigeria’s energy security and accelerate industrial development. The company also plans to grow its production portfolio to one million barrels of oil equivalent per day by 2030, supported by additional gas production and investments in exploration, development and infrastructure-led opportunities. The Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of RAE, Engr. Tony Attah, disclosed this in a keynote address delivered on his behalf by the company’s Vice President, Exploration, Dr. John Bosco Uche, at a pre-conference workshop organised by the Nigerian Association of Petroleum Explorationists (NAPE). The workshop, themed: “Navigating Nigeria’s Upstream Future: Exploration and Development Approaches vs. Energy Security Demand,” examined strategies for increasing petroleum reserves, accelerating project delivery and meeting the country’s growing energy needs. Attah said Nigeria’s energy security depended not merely on its abundant oil and gas resources but on its ability to convert those resources into reliable energy supply, industrial growth, employment and improved living standards. The Renaissance helmsman noted that despite the country’s substantial hydrocarbon resources, millions of Nigerians still lacked reliable access to energy, stressing that the real measure of energy security was the extent to which resources powered homes, industries, hospitals and schools. According to him, exploration, development and production must operate as an integrated value chain to ensure that Nigeria meets its current energy requirements while sustaining supply for future generations. “Exploration creates options. Development transforms options into projects. Production converts projects into energy, and energy security exists only when all these three operate as an integrated value chain,” he said. The Renaissance CEO emphasised the need for continuous investment in exploration to replenish reserves, warning that failure to discover new resources would undermine future production and threaten long-term energy security. He explained that every barrel produced today depended on discoveries and investments made in previous years, making reserve replacement essential to sustaining Nigeria’s petroleum industry. Attah also stressed the importance of accelerating the journey from discovery to first production, arguing that the speed of project delivery had become as important as the volume of resources available. “Energy security is not only about volume; it is about velocity,” he said, adding that discoveries that take decades to reach production could fail to address the immediate energy needs of a growing economy. He identified infrastructure-led exploration as a key strategy for shortening project timelines and improving the commercial value of discoveries, noting that Renaissance had adopted the approach as a central pillar of its near-term strategy. According to him, leveraging existing infrastructure, data and technical knowledge could help unlock additional value from mature assets while reducing the time and cost required to bring resources to market. The company’s strategy, he said, was anchored on three principles: safely receiving inherited assets, stabilising operations and growing production. Attah disclosed that within its first 100 days of assuming operatorship of the assets in March 2025, Renaissance added approximately 100,000 barrels of oil to its portfolio and Nigeria’s production. He added that the company had sustained gas exports while increasing domestic gas supply, with further expansion planned to support the country’s industrialisation and energy needs. On the role of natural gas, Attah described the resource as a major driver of Nigeria’s economic transformation, noting its potential to strengthen manufacturing, improve industrial competitiveness, create jobs and stimulate economic growth. “Gas is not merely a transition fuel for Nigeria; it is our transformation fuel,” he said. He maintained that Nigeria could achieve greater economic benefits by deploying its gas resources to support industrial development and expand access to reliable energy. The Renaissance CEO further highlighted the importance of indigenous capabilities, technology and human capital development in building a sustainable upstream industry. He said the growing participation of indigenous operators represented not just a transfer of assets but also a transfer of responsibility for developing the country’s resources and creating long-term value. Attah also identified artificial intelligence, digital technologies and advanced software as tools for improving exploration decisions, maturing prospects and enhancing operational performance. He said Renaissance had tested several digital solutions and planned to deploy additional technologies to improve the identification and development of exploration opportunities. On workforce development, he announced that the company planned to recruit more than 100 young graduates by November 2026 to strengthen its workforce and contribute to building local technical capacity. He added that sustainable development required the industry to balance environmental responsibility with the need to provide affordable and reliable energy for economic progress. Attah urged industry stakeholders to focus on execution, investment and collaboration, stressing that Nigeria’s petroleum wealth would deliver lasting benefits only when resources were continuously discovered, developed and produced at a pace that matched the country’s energy demand. He concluded that effective leadership with a clear vision and disciplined project execution would be essential to converting the country’s oil and gas potential into energy security, industrialisation and shared prosperity. https://leadership.ng/federal-government.title_zh: 联邦政府制定更广泛的天然气转型战略，以确保稳固的能源安全
https://leadership.ng/federal-government.body_zh: “在这一改革议程中，天然气一直是优先事项，因为各位都知道，尼日利亚的天然气储量甚至比石油储量更加丰富，而天然气可以说是推动工业化最重要的实体资源，”总统石油与天然气特别顾问 Olu Verheijen 表示。她表示，政府目前正在推动天然气生产活动，以保障稳健的能源安全，同时为工业化努力创造价值。Verheijen 在拉各斯举行的 2026 年非洲访谈可持续发展论坛上披露了这些情况。她还表示，自 2026 年 1 月以来，政府已结清超过 ₦100 billion 的天然气欠款，旨在加强天然气发电价值链并改善电力供应。这些付款根据总统电力部门金融改革计划执行；与此同时，尼日利亚继续应对电力供应挑战，天然气供应及向生产商付款仍是电力部门表现的重要因素。清偿拖欠款项预计将增强天然气发电产业链各方的信心，但要实现持续改善，还取决于定期付款、可靠的天然气输送以及电力市场参与者的财务健康状况。Verheijen 还重点介绍了政府自 2023 年以来为鼓励家庭使用液化石油气（LPG）而采取的措施，其中包括对 LPG 和气瓶免征进口关税并实行零税率增值税，以使更清洁的烹饪燃料更容易获得，并减少家庭对柴火的依赖。“一个天然气资源丰富的国家，如果家庭仍然停留在使用柴火的时代，就不可能感到安心，”她说。总统顾问表示，博拉· Tinubu 总统领导下的政府推行改革，旨在消除投资障碍，释放尼日利亚的天然气资源，为工业化、发电和经济增长赋能。她透露，在不到两年的时间里，尼日利亚已有 4 个天然气项目作出最终投资决定（FIDs），日均天然气产量也从约 70 亿立方英尺增至 80 亿立方英尺。Verheijen 表示，尼日利亚拥有超过 200 万亿立方英尺的探明天然气储量，但强调该国必须吸引持续投资，才能将资源基础转化为经济价值。“一个国家可能坐拥巨额自然资源，却未能将其转化为为工业提供动力的能源，无法创造就业，而就业又帮助我们提高收入，”她说。“将资源转化为繁荣的是投资，是回应可预期激励措施和稳定环境的持续投资，”她补充道。Verheijen 表示，Tinubu 已指示政府找出并解决阻碍投资进度未能匹配尼日利亚经济潜力的因素。“博拉· Tinubu 总统于 2023 年就任时，给了我们一项非常明确的指示：查明投资为何未能按照尼日利亚的潜力同步推进，并解决这个问题，”她说。Verheijen 表示，包括 2026 年 9 月 Ima 项目在内的 4 个天然气项目投资决定，反映出该行业活动日益增加。她还指出，本土生产商对国内天然气供应的贡献正在增加。在谈及非洲能源转型时，她认为，非洲各国政府都应在环境可持续性与能源安全、工业发展和创造就业之间实现平衡。“对非洲而言，能源转型必须意味着转型，把分子转化为兆瓦、化肥、石化产品、更清洁的交通、制造业、就业和出口，”她说。Verheijen 还坚持认为，非洲国家应根据自身发展重点和经济状况决定能源转型速度，而不应由外部强加这些决定。“能源转型还必须意味着自主权。非洲有权自行决定以多快速度实现脱碳，而不是让别人替我们作出选择。这关乎确认我们有权书写自己的能源转型篇章，”她说。她进一步强调，需要衡量并减少天然气运营产生的甲烷排放，同时确保东道社区从资源开发中获得切实利益。清偿拖欠的天然气债务，是解决尼日利亚天然气发电价值链内资金限制的一步。然而，更广泛的考验在于，改善后的付款纪律和投资能否带来更可靠的天然气供应、更强的发电能力，以及向家庭和企业更好的供电。与此同时，Renaissance Africa Energy（RAE）表示，正将石油产量提高至 2030 年每天 500,000 桶。这家本土企业还表示，将在实现这一目标的同时扩大天然气供应，作为改善尼日利亚能源安全和加快工业发展的更广泛努力的一部分。公司还计划在勘探、开发和基础设施主导机会方面的投资及新增天然气产量支持下，将生产组合扩大至 2030 年每天 100 万桶油当量。RAE 董事总经理兼首席执行官 Tony Attah 工程博士，在尼日利亚石油勘探家协会（NAPE）组织的会前研讨会上，通过公司勘探副总裁 John Bosco Uche 博士代其发表主旨演讲时披露了上述情况。研讨会的主题为：“把握尼日利亚上游行业的未来：勘探与开发方式对能源安全需求”，会议探讨了增加石油储量、加快项目交付和满足国家日益增长的能源需求等战略。Attah 表示，尼日利亚的能源安全不仅依赖其丰富的石油和天然气资源，也取决于能否将这些资源转化为可靠能源供应、工业增长、就业和更高生活水平。Renaissance 掌舵者指出，尽管该国拥有大量碳氢化合物资源，但数百万尼日利亚人仍无法稳定获得能源，因此真正的能源安全衡量标准，是资源能否为家庭、工业、医院和学校供电。他表示，勘探、开发和生产必须作为整合的价值链运行，以确保尼日利亚满足当前能源需求，同时为后代维持供应。“勘探创造选择，开发把选择转化为项目，生产把项目转化为能源，而只有这三者作为整合价值链运转时，能源安全才存在，”他说。Renaissance 首席执行官强调，需要持续投资勘探以补充储量，并警告未能发现新资源将削弱未来产量，威胁长期能源安全。他解释道，如今产出的每一桶石油都依赖往年取得的发现和投资，因此必须以储量替代来维持尼日利亚石油工业的持续发展。Attah 还强调，加快从发现到首次生产的进程至关重要，认为项目交付速度已与可用资源量同等重要。“能源安全不仅关乎数量，也关乎速度，”他说，并补充称，需要数十年才能投产的新发现，可能无法满足不断增长经济的即时能源需求。他把基础设施主导型勘探列为缩短项目周期和提高发现商业价值的关键战略，并指出 Renaissance 已将这一做法作为近期战略的支柱。他认为，利用现有基础设施、数据和技术知识，有助于从成熟资产中释放更多价值，同时减少将资源推向市场所需的时间和成本。他说，公司的战略以三项原则为基础：安全接收遗留资产、稳定运营以及扩大产量。Attah 透露，自 2025 年 3 月接管这些资产的运营商职责后的前 100 天内，Renaissance 为其生产组合及尼日利亚产量增加了约 100,000 桶石油。他补充说，公司在维持天然气出口的同时增加了国内天然气供应，并计划进一步扩大供应，以支持国家工业化和能源需求。在谈及天然气的作用时，Attah 称其是推动尼日利亚经济转型的重要动力，指出天然气有望强化制造业、提高工业竞争力、创造就业并刺激经济增长。“天然气对尼日利亚而言不仅是过渡燃料，更是我们的转型燃料，”他说。他坚持认为，尼日利亚可以通过利用天然气资源支持工业发展并扩大可靠能源的可及性，获得更大的经济收益。Renaissance 首席执行官还强调，在建设可持续的上游行业时，本土能力、技术和人力资本开发至关重要。他说，本土运营商参与度日益提高，不仅意味着资产转移，也意味着开发国家资源和创造长期价值的责任转移。Attah 还把人工智能、数字技术和先进软件列为改善勘探决策、推进资产成熟及提升运营表现的工具。他说，Renaissance 已测试多种数字解决方案，并计划部署更多技术，以改善勘探机会的识别和开发。在人才队伍建设方面，他宣布，公司计划在 2026 年 11 月前招聘 100 多名年轻毕业生，以加强人才队伍，并为建设本地技术能力作出贡献。他补充称，可持续发展要求行业在环境责任与为经济进步提供价格可承受且可靠的能源之间实现平衡。Attah 敦促行业相关方把重点放在执行、投资与合作上，强调只有以符合国家能源需求的速度持续发现、开发和生产资源，尼日利亚的石油财富才能带来持久利益。他最后表示，有效的领导、清晰的愿景和有纪律的项目执行，将是把该国油气潜力转化为能源安全、工业化和共同繁荣的关键。我们掌握独家优势。订阅 LEADERSHIP NEWS 的 WhatsApp https://leadership.ng/nigeria-gas-associ.summary_zh: 安全问题是尼日利亚液化石油气营销商协会最近一次会议中利益相关方讨论的主要议题之一。该协会还呼吁行业经营者优先重视安全、监管合规和数字化，以推动尼日利亚液化石油气行业实现可持续增长。
https://leadership.ng/nigeria-gas-associ.body: Safety concerns were among major considers among stakeholders at the Nigerian Association of Liquefied Petroleum Gas Marketers (NALPGAM), recent meeting. The association also called on industry operators to prioritise safety, regulatory compliance and digitalisation to drive sustainable growth in Nigeria’s LPG sector. The call followed its 2026 webinar with the theme: “Downstream LPG Operational Excellence and Compliance,” which brought together industry operators, regulators and other stakeholders to address safety risks, market volatility, operational losses and regulatory requirements. Barrister Edu Inyang, National President, NALPGAM, said that “the future of Nigeria’s LPG industry cannot be achieved by increasing volumes alone. We must grow safely, responsibly, efficiently and sustainably. Safety is not an occasional campaign; it must become a continuous industry culture.” A key outcome was the adoption of the aspiration for a “NALPGAM Standard of Operational Excellence,” built on four principles: safe and well-maintained facilities, competent and trained operators, compliant processes, and customer protection. Participants urged operators to embed safety in daily operations, strengthen preventive maintenance, comply with licensing and incident-reporting requirements, and eliminate unsafe practices, including unauthorised propane blending and illegal decanting. “Compliance is not merely a regulatory burden; it is a business advantage. Well-managed LPG operations reduce accidents, improve efficiency, protect investments and strengthen public confidence in our industry,” Inyang said. The webinar also highlighted digital technologies including smart filling systems, automated tank gauges, load cells, flow meters and vehicle tracking as practical tools to reduce product losses, improve accountability and strengthen operational efficiency. With Nigeria targeting LPG consumption of approximately five million tonnes annually by 2030, stakeholders called for increased industry participation in the Decade of Gas LPG penetration programme and stronger collaboration to expand access, improve cylinder traceability and promote certified local manufacturing. NALPGAM further called on regulators and programme coordinators to involve its members in implementing LPG penetration and cylinder recirculation initiatives, leveraging their nationwide reach and proximity to consumers. “Our aspiration is clear: every LPG facility must be safe and properly maintained, every operator competent and adequately trained, every process compliant, and every customer protected. This is the standard of operational excellence we must collectively pursue,” Inyang said. The Association reaffirmed its commitment to constructive engagement with government, regulators and industry stakeholders to build a safer, more efficient and competitive LPG market. NALPGAM’s message is clear: safety must be the industry’s culture, compliance its character, technology its catalyst, and operational excellence its competitive advantage. The association’s push is also coming as the Special Adviser to the President on Oil and Gas, Olu Verheijen, recently highlighted government measures introduced since 2023 to encourage the use of liquefied petroleum gas, LPG, for household cooking. These include import duty waivers and zero-rated value-added tax measures for LPG and gas cylinders, intended to make cleaner cooking alternatives more accessible and reduce dependence on firewood. “A gas-rich nation cannot be comfortable while families remain stuck in the age of firewood,” she told the Africa Interviews Sustainability Forum 2026 in Lagos. https://leadership.ng/nigeria-gas-associ.title_zh: 尼日利亚天然气协会采用标准运营模板，推动尼日利亚液化石油气安全
https://leadership.ng/nigeria-gas-associ.body_zh:
在尼日利亚液化石油气销售商协会最近一次会议上，安全问题是各利益相关方重点考虑的事项之一。该协会还呼吁行业运营商优先重视安全、监管合规和数字化，以推动尼日利亚液化石油气行业实现可持续增长。此次呼吁紧随协会2026年网络研讨会举行，研讨会主题为“液化石油气下游运营卓越与合规”，汇聚行业运营商、监管机构及其他利益相关方，共同应对安全风险、市场波动、运营损失和监管要求。NALPGAM全国主席、律师埃杜·因扬格表示：“尼日利亚液化石油气行业的未来不能仅靠扩大销量来实现。我们必须安全、负责任、高效且可持续地发展。安全不是偶尔开展的宣传活动，而必须成为行业持续不变的文化。”

此次会议的一项主要成果，是通过以四项原则为基础的“NALPGAM运营卓越标准”倡议：设施安全并得到良好维护，运营商具备胜任能力并接受充分培训，流程符合监管要求，以及客户得到保护。参会者敦促运营商将安全融入日常运营，加强预防性维护，遵守许可和事故报告要求，并消除不安全做法，包括未经授权的丙烷混装和非法罐装倒卖。

因扬格说：“合规不仅是监管负担，更是商业优势。管理良好的液化石油气运营可以减少事故、提高效率、保护投资，并增强公众对本行业的信心。”

网络研讨会还重点介绍了智能灌装系统、自动储罐计量仪、称重传感器、流量计和车辆追踪等数字技术，将其视为减少产品损失、提高问责度和增强运营效率的实用工具。尼日利亚的目标是到2030年将液化石油气年消费量提高至约500万吨，各利益相关方呼吁更多行业运营商参与“天然气十年液化石油气普及计划”，并加强合作，以扩大供应可及性、改善气瓶可追溯性并推动获得认证的本地制造。NALPGAM还呼吁监管机构和计划协调方，在实施液化石油气普及和气瓶循环使用计划时让协会成员参与其中，发挥其全国覆盖网络以及贴近消费者的优势。

因扬格说：“我们的目标很明确：每一处液化石油气设施都必须安全并得到适当维护，每一名运营商都必须具备胜任能力并接受充分培训，每一道流程都必须合规，每一位客户都必须受到保护。这就是我们必须共同追求的运营卓越标准。”

该协会重申，将继续与政府、监管机构和行业利益相关方开展建设性合作，以打造更安全、更高效且更具竞争力的液化石油气市场。NALPGAM传达的信息十分明确：安全必须成为行业文化，合规必须成为行业品格，技术必须成为行业催化剂，而运营卓越必须成为行业竞争优势。

就在该协会推动这些工作的同时，总统石油与天然气特别顾问奥卢·弗赫伊恩最近介绍了政府自2023年以来为鼓励家庭烹饪使用液化石油气而出台的措施。这些措施包括对液化石油气和燃气瓶实行进口关税豁免及零税率增值税，旨在让更清洁的烹饪选择更加容易获得，并减少家庭对柴火的依赖。她在拉各斯举行的“非洲访谈可持续论坛2026”上表示：“一个天然气资源丰富的国家，不能在家庭仍被困于柴火时代的情况下感到安心。”

https://leadership.ng/kingibe-taps-into-.summary: Senator Kingibe’s warning that Nigeria’s new tax laws will compel citizens to surrender 25 per cent of their earnings to the government has ignited a debate extending beyond taxation. During an election period, the factual basis of the senator’s assertion may prove secondary as she taps into the sentiments Nigerians generally feel about the new tax laws and economic reforms of the president’s administration. Kingibe’s position as a senator gives her claims institutional visibility.
https://leadership.ng/kingibe-taps-into-.summary_zh: 参议员金吉比警告称，尼日利亚新税法将迫使公民把收入的25%交给政府，由此引发了一场超出税收本身的讨论。在选举时期，这位参议员言论的事实依据可能显得次要，因为她利用了尼日利亚民众对新税法以及总统政府经济改革的普遍情绪。金吉比担任参议员，使其主张获得了制度层面的关注。
https://leadership.ng/kingibe-taps-into-.body: It can be seen in the ease with which laws are passed, from the tax reform bills to the 2026 Electoral Act. That only changes when lawmakers are faced with defending their seats from outside the ruling party. And a lot is going on in the economy for opposition lawmakers to focus on. Senator Ireti Kingine, an opposition lawmaker representing the FCT, chose one of the most contentious laws passed by the National Assembly to strike at the ruling party, its newly introduced tax laws. Senator Kingibe’s warning that Nigeria’s new tax laws will compel citizens to surrender 25 per cent of their earnings to the government has ignited a debate extending beyond taxation. The reality is that only the highest-income earners pay that level of personal tax, while the lowest-income earners are expected to pay between 0 and 18 per cent. Regardless of accuracy, its rapid circulation reflects the declining public confidence in economic policies introduced under President Bola Tinubu’s government. It also exposes how economic anxiety can amplify political messaging and become a handy weapon to turn voters against the ruling party. During an election period, the factual basis of the senator’s assertion may prove secondary as she taps into the sentiments Nigerians generally feel about the new tax laws and economic reforms of the president’s administration. Here is why her warning resonates. Nigerians are confronting the cumulative consequences of petrol subsidy removal, currency depreciation, rising living costs, and electricity tariffs. Against this backdrop, taxation can appear less like an instrument of public finance and more like another demand on already strained household incomes. Kingibe’s position as a senator gives her claims institutional visibility. Nevertheless, even a claim made for political ends can intensify perceptions of hardship. Many Nigerians, small business owners, and manufacturers already distrust government assurances, while the tweaking of facts and interpretations can reinforce existing fears. For the opposition, particularly the ADC to which Senator Kingibe belongs and is seeking reelection, these issues offer legitimate grounds for scrutinising the government. Fuel subsidy removal, taxation, foreign borrowing, and monetary policy all deserve rigorous examination. The challenge is to connect them to verifiable evidence, measurable outcomes, and credible alternatives. Ultimately, Kingibe’s intervention highlights both the opportunity and danger facing Nigeria’s opposition. The decisive question is not whether Nigerians are angry. It is whether political leaders can translate that anger into informed debate about who bears economic costs, how government spends public resources, and what realistic alternatives exist. Then there is an even bigger issue. The fact that many Nigerian voters don’t see the contradiction in the economic hardship they are going through, and their willingness to sell their votes to the same political party that has engineered their suffering. https://leadership.ng/audu-confronts-ind.summary: Nigeria’s Ministry of Steel Development is on the path of bureaucratic redundancy: an institution whose industrial ambitions remain disconnected from the country’s manufacturing reality. Yet Ajaokuta Steel Company remains the enduring symbol of industrial failure. Audu can point to investment promotion, a commissioned steel-processing facility, and agreements aimed at reviving dormant industrial assets.
https://leadership.ng/audu-confronts-ind.summary_zh: 尼日利亚钢铁发展部正陷入机构冗余：其工业抱负与该国制造业现实仍然脱节。然而，Ajaokuta钢铁公司依然是工业失败的持久象征。Audu可以列举出推动投资的工作、一座已投入运营的钢材加工设施，以及旨在振兴闲置工业资产的协议。
https://leadership.ng/audu-confronts-ind.body: Nigeria’s Ministry of Steel Development is on the path of bureaucratic redundancy: an institution whose industrial ambitions remain disconnected from the country’s manufacturing reality. Since 1999, successive governments have promised to transform Nigeria into a steel-producing nation. Under Olusegun Obasanjo, Olu Agunloye served as minister of power and steel, followed by Olusegun Agagu. Subsequent administrations brought ministers including Sarafa Ishola, Diezani Alison-Madueke, Musa Sada, Kayode Fayemi, Abubakar Bawa Bwari, Olamilekan Adegbite, and, since 2023, Shuaibu Audu. Yet Ajaokuta Steel Company remains the enduring symbol of industrial failure. Audu can point to investment promotion, a commissioned steel-processing facility, and agreements aimed at reviving dormant industrial assets. But these achievements should not be equated with rebuilding Nigeria’s integrated steel industry. The problem transcends individual ministers. Abandoned projects, inadequate infrastructure, unreliable electricity, and governance failures have undermined successive revival efforts. Billions have been discussed, investors have been courted, and technical assessments have been commissioned, but Nigeria still struggles to translate its iron ore deposits into competitive domestic steel production. Aliko Dangote briefly offered hope in 2024, announcing plans to enter steel production and supply West Africa. Two months later, he abandoned the proposal, citing concerns that his investment would attract accusations of monopoly, preferring instead to invest in power generation. It was a curious choice, considering that he has invested in a vehicle assembly plant and needs earth-moving equipment more than any other industrialist. Nevertheless, his withdrawal exposed a troubling investment climate in which even ambitious domestic capital may hesitate to pursue strategic industrial projects. Egypt’s established steelmakers and vehicle-assembly operations demonstrate how domestic production can support industrial value chains, although neither country manufactures everything it consumes. Steel alone does not manufacture cars, ships, or weapons. Skilled engineers, reliable energy, technology, financing, and sustained industrial policy are equally essential. Nevertheless, without competitively priced steel, Nigeria’s ambitions in shipbuilding, vehicle manufacturing, construction, and defence production incur additional costs and become more dependent on imports. Audu and the ministry he heads can only be measured by outcomes, not announcements. Can he restore viable production, attract credible investors, and establish transparent, time-bound targets? Until Nigerians see steel plants operating competitively, the ministry will remain vulnerable to an uncomfortable question: what, precisely, has it delivered for industrialisation? https://leadership.ng/audu-confronts-ind.body_zh: 尼日利亚钢铁发展部正走向机构冗余：其工业抱负与该国制造业现实仍然脱节。自1999年以来，历届政府都承诺要将尼日利亚打造为钢铁生产国。在奥卢塞贡·奥巴桑乔执政期间，奥卢·阿贡洛耶担任电力与钢铁部长，之后是奥卢塞贡·阿加古。此后的历届政府先后任命了萨拉法·伊绍拉、迪耶扎尼·艾利森-马杜埃克、穆萨·萨达、卡约德·费耶米、阿布巴卡尔·巴瓦-布瓦里、奥拉米莱坎·阿德格比特以及自2023年起任职的舒艾布·奥杜担任部长。然而，阿贾奥库塔钢铁公司仍是工业失败的标志性象征。奥杜可以列举促进投资、建成一座钢铁加工设施，以及达成旨在振兴闲置工业资产的协议等成果。但这些成就不能与重建尼日利亚一体化钢铁产业混为一谈。问题超越了历任部长个人。废弃项目、基础设施不足、电力供应不稳定和治理失效，削弱了一轮又一轮振兴努力。数十亿规模的资金曾被讨论，投资者曾受到招揽，技术评估也曾得到委托，但尼日利亚仍难以将自身的铁矿石储量转化为具有竞争力的国产钢材。阿里科·丹戈特在2024年曾短暂带来希望，宣布计划进入钢铁生产领域并供应西非。两个月后，他放弃了该计划，称担心自己的投资会招致垄断指控，转而选择投资电力生产。考虑到他已投资一家汽车装配厂，而且比任何其他工业家都更需要土方机械，这一选择颇为耐人寻味。尽管如此，他的退出暴露出令人不安的投资环境：即使是雄心勃勃的本土资本，也可能对推进战略性工业项目有所顾虑。埃及成熟的钢铁企业和汽车装配业务表明，本土生产能够支撑工业价值链，尽管两国都不生产全部所需物资。仅靠钢铁无法制造汽车、船舶或武器。熟练工程师、可靠能源、技术、融资和持续连贯的工业政策同样不可或缺。然而，如果没有价格具有竞争力的钢材，尼日利亚在造船、汽车制造、建筑和国防生产方面的雄心就会承担额外成本，并对进口产生更高依赖。奥杜及其领导的部门只能以成果而非公告来衡量。他能否恢复可行的生产、吸引可信的投资者，并设定透明且有时限的目标？在尼日利亚人看到钢铁厂以具有竞争力的方式投入运营之前，该部门仍难逃避一个令人不安的问题：它究竟为工业化带来了什么？我们掌握最新动态。获取实时报道、突发独家消息和独家视角，直接推送到您的手机。不要满足于陈旧新闻。加入LEADERSHIP NEWS，通过WhatsApp获取全天候更新 →

https://leadership.ng/csos-activists-fau.summary: He noted that the reported remarks were particularly concerning given Omo-Agege’s former position as Deputy Senate President, stressing that political leaders had a responsibility to respect constitutional institutions and promote peaceful democratic participation.
https://leadership.ng/csos-activists-fau.summary_zh: 他指出，鉴于Omo-Agege曾任参议院副议长，所报道的言论尤其令人担忧。他强调，政治领导人有责任尊重宪法机构，并推动和平参与民主活动。
https://leadership.ng/csos-activists-fau.body: The Senator, who is seeking to represent Delta Central Senatorial District under the NDC, made the remarks at a political event in his constituency ON Friday. “I want to make the news again. Anybody who rigs the election on that day, we will kill him! If you don’t value your life, come and rig the election,” he vowed. The groups have expressed concern over the reported remarks alongside the suggestion that electoral disputes should no longer be taken to court, warning that such rhetoric could heighten political tension, undermine democratic institutions and expose citizens to violence. In an exclusive interview with LEADERSHIP Weekend, CISLAC executive director and head of Transparency International Nigeria, Auwal Musa Rafsanjani, described the reported remarks as dangerous and incompatible with democratic leadership. Rafsanjani said electoral fraud was a criminal offence that must be addressed through lawful processes rather than threats of extrajudicial punishment. “No politician has the authority to determine who lives or dies,” he said, warning that inflammatory political statements could embolden violent actors at a time when Nigeria was grappling with insecurity, electoral distrust and persistent political thuggery. He noted that the reported remarks were particularly concerning given Omo-Agege’s former position as Deputy Senate President, stressing that political leaders had a responsibility to respect constitutional institutions and promote peaceful democratic participation. According to CISLAC, Nigerians’ growing frustration with electoral manipulation, compromised institutions and prolonged judicial processes should lead to urgent reforms rather than calls for mob justice. The organisation maintained that electoral credibility could not be restored by abandoning the rule of law, insisting that electoral offenders must be investigated, prosecuted and sanctioned through transparent and impartial processes. CISLAC called on the Nigeria Police Force to investigate the reported remarks and determine whether they violated any laws. It also urged INEC to enforce applicable electoral regulations, while calling on political parties to demonstrate zero tolerance for inflammatory statements and electoral intimidation. The organisation further urged security agencies to act impartially and ensure that political influence did not obstruct accountability. In a statement signed by its founder and executive director, Amarachi Evangel Okeke, the organisation said electoral integrity must be protected and attempts to manipulate the will of voters firmly resisted, but stressed that threats of death and violence were not acceptable means of defending democracy. It maintained that electoral accountability must be pursued through lawful, peaceful and credible processes, adding that no political ambition was worth the loss of human life. WIELD-I warned that threatening political rhetoric could create an atmosphere of fear among citizens, electoral officials, observers and political opponents, potentially discouraging them from exercising their democratic rights. The organisation expressed particular concern about the implications for women and other groups already facing barriers to political participation. It said the association of politics with threats and violence could discourage qualified women from contesting elections, restrict citizens’ participation and further weaken democratic inclusion. WIELD-I urged political leaders and candidates across party lines to exercise restraint, demonstrate responsibility and communicate their positions without threats or incitement. It also called on relevant authorities to assess the reported statement in accordance with the law and take appropriate action where necessary. The organisation emphasised that credible elections required more than preventing electoral fraud, noting that disputes must be resolved through lawful procedures, citizens must be able to participate without fear, and every eligible voter’s choice must be respected. Both organisations stressed that the 2027 general elections must be characterised by electoral integrity, institutional accountability and respect for the rule of law. They urged political leaders seeking public office to uphold the Constitution, protect citizens and promote peaceful participation in the democratic process. “Democracy must be defended through the ballot, not the bullet,” CISLAC maintained. The threat by Senator Ovie Omo-Agege that election riggers ahead of the 2027 general elections could face deadly consequences has led to disagreements among stakeholders. Meanwhile, Comrade Victor Ojei, AKA Wong Box, Lead Activist for the Young Nigerian Rights Organization, (YNRO), also, Delta North Senatorial Candidate under Action Peoples Party, (APP) said the statement is not a sign of courage but a dangerous reflection of how desperate Nigerian politicians have become. He said Omo-Agege cannot spend years benefiting from a corrupt political system, remain silent when it favours you, and suddenly pretend to be a saint when it no longer serves your ambition. “His political history, from the PDP to the APC and now the NDC, raises serious questions about consistency and political convenience. Democracy is not a do-or-die affair, and no election is worth a human life. Those who helped weaken public confidence in our electoral system cannot suddenly become champions of electoral justice simply because the system has turned against them. “The same political establishment has contributed to voter apathy, leaving competent citizens discouraged and allowing mediocrity to thrive. The real tragedy is that these politicians are not fighting for the common man; too often, they are fighting for their own survival and relevance. Delta state does not need recycled politicians with recycled promises. It needs credible, competent and selfless leaders. According to him, “as we approach 2027, Deltans must wake up! Do not vote blindly because of party affiliation, personality cults or the Peter Obi wave. Vote for character, competence, credibility and proven capacity. A party is not a certificate of good leadership, and an old political name is not proof of public service. “Shame on every politician who helped corrupt our democracy but now cries foul when the same system refuses to serve their ambition. Our votes must count, but our lives must never become the price of political ambition. Asking, “are Nigerian youths ready to break free from the political stockholm syndrome that makes people defend the very establishment responsible for their suffering? Until we reject political manipulation and demand accountability, the same old players will keep recycling themselves while the masses remain trapped in poverty. He stated that 2027 must be about the people, not the politicians, enough of political slavery, enough of recycled failures, saying the future belongs to those who dare to demand better” Ojei stated. But Sunny Areh, Media Adviser to Senator Ovie Omo-Agege said Omo-Agege’s warning to election riggers was a deterrent against electoral fraud. Areh stated that Senator Omo-Agege’s position aligned with President Bola Tinubu’s recent directive to security agencies to ensure free, fair and credible elections in 2027. Tinubu directed security agencies to do their work. Omo-Agege is only enforcing that directive at the grassroots. Areh said the senator spoke the minds of average Nigerian voters frustrated by 24 years of electoral manipulation, saying election rigging amounts to armed robbery against the people, riggers steal not just votes but the future of citizens. “If a man enters your house with a gun to steal your TV, we call him an armed robber. If a man enters your polling unit with a gun to steal your future and your children’s future, we call him a stakeholder? No. Riggers don’t just rig figures, they rig hospitals, roads and schools. “The disgraceful advice to aggrieved politicians to “go to court” has emboldened riggers, who use proceeds of rigged mandates to hire lawyers to frustrate justice on technical grounds, such as failure to file Certified True Copies”. “If you don’t plan to rig, why are you offended by ‘rig and die’? If you don’t plan to steal, why are you afraid of ‘aura for aura” According to him, Senator Omo-Agege’s warning is likened to “Beware of Dogs” sign on a gate, meant to deter thieves and not to threaten innocent passersby. https://leadership.ng/csos-activists-fau.title_zh: 民间社会组织和活动人士批评奥莫阿格格就选举舞弊发出死亡威胁
https://leadership.ng/csos-activists-fau.body_zh:
这位参议员以国家民主党的名义竞选三角洲州中部参议员选区代表，于星期五在其选区的一场政治活动上发表了上述言论。他说：“我想再次成为新闻焦点。任何在那一天操纵选举的人，我们都会杀了谁！如果你不珍惜自己的生命，就来操纵选举吧。”他誓言要这样做。

继这番言论被报道后，相关团体对有关言论以及“选举争议不应再诉诸法院”的建议表示担忧，并警告称，此类言论可能加剧政治紧张，破坏民主制度，使公民面临暴力风险。

CISLAC执行主任、透明国际尼日利亚负责人Auwal Musa Rafsanjani在接受《LEADERSHIP》周末版独家采访时，将有关言论描述为危险的，而且与民主领导格格不入。Rafsanjani表示，选举舞弊属于刑事犯罪，必须通过合法程序处理，而不是以法外惩罚的威胁来处理。

他说：“任何政治人物都无权决定谁生谁死。”他警告称，在尼日利亚正面临安全局势紧张、对选举的不信任以及政治暴徒活动长期持续之际，煽动性的政治言论可能助长暴力行为者。他指出，鉴于Omo-Agege此前担任副参议长的职位，有关言论尤其令人担忧，并强调政治领导人有责任尊重宪政机构，促进和平的民主参与。

CISLAC表示，尼日利亚人对选举操弄、机构失灵和司法程序旷日持久的日益不满，应推动紧急改革，而不是calls for mob justice。该组织坚持认为，放弃法治无法恢复选举公信力，选举违法者必须接受调查、起诉和制裁，而且整个过程应透明、公正。

CISLAC呼吁尼日利亚警察部队调查有关言论，并确定其是否违反任何法律。它还敦促INEC执行适用的选举法规，同时呼吁各政党对煽动性言论和选举恐吓行为实行零容忍。该组织进一步敦促安全机构公正行事，确保政治影响力不会妨碍问责。

该组织在一份由创始人兼执行主任Amarachi Evangel Okeke签署的声明中表示，必须保护选举诚信，坚决抵制操纵选民意志的行为，但强调，威胁使用死亡和暴力并不是捍卫民主的可接受手段。该组织坚持认为，选举问责必须通过合法、和平和可信的程序推进，任何政治野心都不值得以人的生命为代价。

WIELD-I警告称，威胁性的政治言论可能在公民、选举工作人员、观察员和政治对手之间制造恐惧氛围，挫伤他们行使民主权利的意愿。该组织对妇女及其他已经面临政治参与障碍的群体所受影响的潜在风险尤其感到担忧。它表示，将政治与威胁和暴力相联系，可能使有能力的女性不愿参加选举，限制公民参与，并进一步削弱民主包容性。

WIELD-I敦促各党派政治领导人和候选人保持克制、承担责任，在不进行威胁或煽动的情况下表达立场。它还呼吁相关当局依照法律评估有关声明，并在必要时采取适当行动。

该组织强调，可信的选举不仅仅需要防止选举舞弊，争议必须通过合法程序解决，公民必须能够在没有恐惧的情况下参与，每一位合格选民的选择都必须得到尊重。

两个组织都强调，2027年大选必须体现选举诚信、机构问责和对法治的尊重。它们敦促争取公职的政治领导人遵守宪法、保护公民，并促进公众和平参与民主进程。

CISLAC坚持认为：“民主必须通过选票来捍卫，而不是通过子弹。”

参议员Ovie Omo-Agege威胁称，在2027年大选前操纵选举的人可能面临致命后果，这已在利益相关方之间引发分歧。与此同时，青年尼日利亚权利组织（YNRO）首席活动人士、APP三角洲州北部参议员候选人Victor Ojei（又名Wong Box）表示，这番言论并非勇气的表现，而是对尼日利亚政治人物何等绝望的危险反映。

他说，Omo-Agege不能一边多年来从腐败政治体系中获益，在体系对己有利时保持沉默，一边又在体系不再服务于其政治野心时突然假装成圣人。

他说：“他从人民民主党（PDP）转投全民大会党（APC），如今又加入国家民主党（NDC），这段政治经历对政策的一贯性和政治 opportunism提出了严重疑问。民主不是一场生死决战，任何选举都不值得牺牲人的生命。那些曾帮助削弱公众对我国选举制度信任的人，不能仅仅因为该制度不再对自己有利，就突然成为选举正义的捍卫者。

“同一套政治建制助长了选民冷漠，使能干公民灰心，并纵容平庸之辈。真正的悲剧在于，这些政治人物并不是为普通人而战；他们往往是在为自己的生存和存在价值而战。三角洲州不需要不断重复自己、重复承诺的旧政客。它需要可信、能干且无私的领导人。

据他表示：“随着2027年临近，三角洲州居民必须醒醒！不要因为党派归属、个人崇拜或Peter Obi浪潮而盲目投票。要把选票投给品格、能力、可信度和经过证明的执政能力。政党不是良好领导的证明证书，资深的政治名号也不是公共服务业绩的凭证。

“每个曾帮助败坏我国民主、如今又在同一制度拒绝满足其野心时高喊不公的政治人物都应感到羞耻。我们的选票必须算数，但我们的生命绝不能成为政治野心的代价。”

他问道：“尼日利亚青年是否已经准备好摆脱政治斯德哥尔摩综合征，不再为那个导致他们受苦的建制辩护？在我们拒绝政治操弄并要求问责之前，那帮老面孔仍会不断包装自己，而大众则继续困在贫困之中。”

他表示，2027年必须以人民为中心，而不是以政治人物为中心；政治奴役够了，反复包装的失败者也够了，未来属于那些敢于要求更好未来的人。Ojei表示。

然而，参议员Ovie Omo-Agege的媒体顾问Sunny Areh表示，Omo-Agege对选举操弄者的警告是遏制选举舞弊的手段。Areh表示，参议员Ovie Omo-Agege的立场与总统Bola Tinubu近期指示安全机构确保2027年选举自由、公平和可信的要求一致。Tinubu已指示安全机构履行职责，而Omo-Agege只是在基层落实这一指示。

Areh称，参议员说出了那些因24年选举操弄而感到沮丧的普通尼日利亚选民的心声，并表示，操纵选举无异于对人民实施武装抢劫，操弄者偷走的不只是选票，还有公民的未来。

“如果一个人持枪闯入你家 stealing your TV，我们称他为武装强盗。如果一个人持枪闯入你的投票站，偷走你和你孩子的未来，我们却称他为利益相关者吗？不。操弄者操纵的不只是数字，还包括医院、道路和学校。

“建议那些感到不满的政治人物‘去法院起诉’这种可耻建议，反而助长了操弄者；他们利用操纵选票获得的职位收益聘请律师，以未提交认证副本等技术性理由阻碍正义。

“如果不打算操纵选举，你为什么会因‘操纵就得死’而生气？如果不打算偷窃，你为什么会害怕‘以牙还牙’？”

据他表示，参议员Omo-Agege的警告就像大门上的“当心恶犬”警示牌，其目的是震慑盗贼，而不是威胁无辜路人。

三角洲州中部选民的意愿将在2027年占据上风，每一票都将算数。我们占据优势。

https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/25/y.body: The presidential candidate of Young Progressives Party (YPP), Mr Peter Agada, has faulted the federal government’s 90-day action plan to ease cost of living, describing it as a campaign strategy that did not reflect economic reality. Agada said the President Bola Tinubu’s administration had failed after introducing numerous economic measures without results. The Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of Economy, Mr. Taiwo Oyedele, had announced that the National Executive Council (NEC) approved a 90-day plan to cushion the high cost of living on Nigerians. Reacting in an interview in Abuja, Agada said the economic team of the President had lost focus. “I align with those who opine that the economic team of Mr. President has failed to address Nigeria’s numerous economic challenges. I have listened to many analysts, but none spoke positively in support of the economic team,” he said. He noted that the minister had earlier announced subsidy intervention and a 17-point plan, including reduction of pump price, removal of illegal levies, but nothing was done, prompting resort to a 90-day timeline. “These promises back and forth are for Nigerians to believe and vote them back into office. If you believe in the rules of the game they are playing, there are just 85 days to election, and you are saying a 90-day timeline to cushion the cost of living. So, after the election, what happens? These guys are playing mind games,” he said. He said the government later removed tariffs on food importation which did not fight food inflation but only affected calculation. “If you said you were fighting food inflation, then return food prices to where they were before you took office,” he said. He further alleged that import waiver cuts pushed customs revenue to N35 trillion with about 60 per cent for military hardware importation without accounting. As an alternative, Agada recommended his Labour-Direct ward-to-ward development strategy, which he said can empower Nigerians with N40 million monthly and capture all Nigerians within 60 days of implementation. “Labour-Direct, ward-to-ward strategy remains an option that can capture all Nigerians within 60 days. At the moment, they have to take a look at our ward-to-ward plan. If they approach me to implement a 60-day development plan, Nigerians will have more confidence,” he said. https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/25/y.title_zh: YPP总统候选人Agada指责FG实施90日行动计划以缓解生活成本压力
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/25/y.body_zh: 青年进步党（YPP）总统候选人彼得·阿加达指责联邦政府为缓解生活成本而推出的90天行动计划，称其是一项没有反映经济现实的竞选策略。阿加达表示，博拉·蒂努布总统政府推出多项经济措施却毫无成果，已经失败。财政部长兼经济协调部长塔伊沃·奥耶德莱此前宣布，全国执行委员会（NEC）批准了一项90天计划，以缓冲尼日利亚人的高昂生活成本。阿加达在阿布贾接受采访时表示，总统的经济团队已经失去重点。他说：“我赞同那些认为总统先生的经济团队未能应对尼日利亚众多经济挑战的人。我听了许多分析人士的意见，但没有一人积极评价并支持这个经济团队。”他指出，部长此前曾宣布要采取补贴干预措施并推出一项17点计划，包括下调泵价、取消非法收费，但政府并未采取任何行动，因此转而采用90天时限。“这些反复作出的承诺，是为了让尼日利亚人相信他们，并投票让他们重新掌权。如果您相信他们正在遵循的规则，那么距离选举只剩85天，他们却提出用90天来缓冲生活成本。那么，选举之后又会怎样？这些人在玩心理游戏。”他说，政府后来取消食品进口关税，但这并未遏制食品通胀，只是影响了计算结果。“如果您说自己在遏制食品通胀，那就把食品价格恢复到你上任前的水平。”他还指控，进口豁免削减令海关收入降至35万亿奈拉，其中约60%用于进口军事装备，而且没有进行核算。作为替代方案，阿加达建议推行其“劳工直达”社区逐区发展战略。他称，该战略每月可为尼日利亚人带来4000万奈拉，并在实施后60天内覆盖全体尼日利亚人。他说：“‘劳工直达’逐区战略仍是一个可以在60天内覆盖全体尼日利亚人的选择。眼下，他们必须审视我们的逐区计划。如果他们来找我实施60天发展计划，尼日利亚人就会更有信心。”THISDAY于1995年1月22日创刊，由THISDAY NEWSPAPERS LTD.出版，地址为尼日利亚拉各斯阿帕帕克里克路35号，在尼日利亚36个州、联邦首都辖区及世界各地设有办公室。作为尼日利亚最权威的新闻媒体，该报通过所有平台服务于政治、商业、专业和外交精英以及更广泛的中产阶级，同时为有志者、千禧一代提供新思想、文化与技术的交汇点。这份报纸是一项公共信任，致力于追求真相与理性，报道范围涵盖突发新闻、政治、商业、金融市场、艺术、体育和社区，以及人与社会的交汇点。您可以发送邮件至：hello@thisdaylive.com，或访问我们的联系我们页面

https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/25/c.summary: The President of the Congress of University Academics (CONUA), Dr. Niyi Sunmonu, has warned that the union will pursue appropriate lawful trade union actions if the federal government fails to conclude its Collective Bargaining Agreement without further delay. In the same vein, the Secretary General of the Trade Union Congress of Nigeria (TUC), Dr. Nuhu Toro, has demanded immediate action to finalise the collective bargaining agreement with CONUA.
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/25/c.summary_zh: 大学教师工会大会（CONUA）主席Niyi Sunmoni博士警告称，如果联邦政府未能尽快敲定集体谈判协议，该工会将采取适当的合法工会行动。与此同时，尼日利亚工会大会（TUC）秘书长Nuhu Toro博士要求立即采取行动，与CONUA敲定集体谈判协议。
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/25/c.body: The President of the Congress of University Academics (CONUA), Dr. Niyi Sunmonu, has warned that the union will pursue appropriate lawful trade union actions if the federal government fails to conclude its Collective Bargaining Agreement without further delay. In the same vein, the Secretary General of the Trade Union Congress of Nigeria (TUC), Dr. Nuhu Toro, has demanded immediate action to finalise the collective bargaining agreement with CONUA. Sunmonu gave the warning yesterday in Abuja while addressing journalists after the National Executive Council (NEC) meeting of the union held at the University of Abuja. He said NEC reviewed the latest draft of the proposed FGN-CONUA Agreement of September 2026 and condemned the failure of the federal government to treat CONUA fairly. “CONUA has consistently pursued constructive engagement and believe that dialogue must lead to tangible outcomes. The recognition of a trade union must translate into meaningful collective bargaining and a concluded agreement that provides an effective framework for representing its members,” Sunmonu said. He called on the Federal Ministries of Education and Labour and Employment, and all relevant negotiating authorities, to conclude the process as a mark of government’s commitment to democratic process and sustained industrial harmony in Nigerian universities. “While CONUA remains committed to dialogue, the union reserves the right to pursue appropriate lawful trade union actions in pursuit of the welfare of its members, should the circumstances warrant it,” the CONUA President warned. He also demanded the prompt settlement of outstanding entitlements, including three and a half months of withheld salaries, promotion arrears, irregular payment of recently approved entitlements and arrears arising from the 25% and 35% wage awards. “University academics must not be subjected to indefinite delays, the trauma resulting from trivialization of its well-being and inconsistent implementation or administrative uncertainty,” he said. He commended the federal government for resolving the pension-entitlement issue, recalling the collaborative programme organised by CONUA and PENCOM on 26 September 2024. On representation, Sunmonu said CONUA’s exclusion from programmes associated with TETFund and NEEDS Assessment was unfair. On university education, the CONUA President said Nigeria cannot build a competitive knowledge economy on inadequately funded and poorly equipped universities. He called for reliable electricity, internet connectivity, functional laboratories and digital transformation, while condemning reported practices of hiring or renting academic staff and equipment for accreditation. “Accreditation must reflect an institution’s genuine and sustainable capacity to deliver its programmes. It must not become an exercise in appearances that conceal deficiencies in staffing, facilities or equipment,” Sunmonu stated. Meanwhile, the Secretary General of the TUC, Dr. Toro, has demanded immediate action to finalize the collective bargaining agreement with CONUA. Toro, who spoke on behalf of the TUC leadership said the congress would not tolerate any unnecessary delay by the relevant university authorities and government agencies responsible for concluding and signing the agreement. According to him, collective bargaining agreements are not political favours or administrative conveniences, but serious commitments that must be respected in accordance with the laws of the land. Toro further declared the solidarity of the TUC with CONUA, saying the university academics must not stand apart from the wider struggles of the Nigerian working class. “CONUA must not stand alone in defending university academics and university academics must not stand apart from the wider struggles of the national working class,” he said. https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/25/c.title_zh: CONUA要求FG立即敲定协议，否则将采取行动
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/25/c.body_zh: 大学教师大会（CONUA）主席尼伊·松莫努博士警告，如果联邦政府仍不尽快完成集体谈判协议，该工会将采取适当的合法工会行动。与此同时，尼日利亚工会大会（TUC）秘书长努胡·托罗博士要求立即采取行动，最终敲定与CONUA达成的集体谈判协议。松莫努昨天在阿布贾发表讲话时作出上述警告。此前，工会全国执行委员会（NEC）在阿贾大学举行会议，他在接受记者采访时说，NEC审议了拟议中的2026年9月联邦政府—CONUA协议最新草案，并谴责联邦政府未能公平对待CONUA。松莫努说：“CONUA始终致力于建设性沟通，并认为对话必须带来切实成果。对工会的承认必须转化为有意义的集体谈判，以及一项已经达成并能为代表工会成员提供有效框架的协议。”他呼吁联邦教育与劳工部、联邦就业与劳工部以及所有相关谈判机构完成协议谈判进程，以体现政府对民主程序以及尼日利亚大学持续保持工业和谐的承诺。CONUA主席警告说：“尽管CONUA仍致力于对话，但如果情况需要，工会保留采取适当合法工会行动的权利，以维护成员福祉。”他还要求迅速解决尚未兑现的权益，包括被扣发的3个半月工资、晋升欠款、近期获批权益的不规范支付，以及根据25%和35%工资决定产生的欠款。他说：“大学教师不应遭受无限期拖延，也不应因自身福祉被轻视以及执行不一致或行政管理不确定而受到创伤。”他赞扬联邦政府解决了养老金权益问题，并提到由CONUA和PENCOM于2024年9月26日组织的协作项目。在代表权问题上，松莫努说，将CONUA排除在与TETFund相关项目和NEEDS评估之外是不公平的。在大学教育方面，CONUA主席指出，尼日利亚无法依靠资金不足、设备落后的大学建设具有竞争力的知识经济。他呼吁提供稳定电力、网络连接、正常运转的实验室并推进数字化转型，同时谴责有报道称，为取得认证而雇用或租用教学人员和设备的做法。松莫努表示：“认证必须反映一所机构提供其课程的真实且可持续的能力，绝不能沦为掩饰人员、设施或设备缺陷的表面文章。”与此同时，TUC秘书长托罗博士要求立即采取行动，最终敲定与CONUA达成的集体谈判协议。托罗代表TUC领导层发言说，大会绝不容忍负责完成和签署协议的相关大学主管部门及政府机构无谓拖延。据他介绍，集体谈判协议不是政治恩惠或行政便利，而是必须依照国家法律予以履行的严肃承诺。托罗进一步声明，TUC声援CONUA，并表示大学教师不能置身于尼日利亚劳动阶级的更广泛斗争之外。他说：“CONUA在捍卫大学教师权益时不能孤立作战，大学教师也不能置身于全国劳动阶级更广泛的斗争之外。”THISDAY于1995年1月22日创办，由THISDAY NEWSPAPERS LTD.出版，地址为尼日利亚拉各斯阿帕帕溪路35号，在尼日利亚36个州、联邦首都辖区及世界各地设有办公室。作为尼日利亚最权威的新闻媒体，该报通过所有平台服务政治、商业、专业和外交精英以及更广泛的中产阶层，同时成为有抱负者和千禧一代的新思想、文化与技术交汇点。这份报纸是一项公共信托，致力于追求真相与理性，报道范围涵盖突发新闻、政治、商业、金融市场、艺术、体育、社区以及人与社会的交叉地带。您可以发送邮件至：hello@thisdaylive.com，或访问我们的联系我们页面

https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/25/s.body: The Governor of Anambra State, Prof. Chukwuma Soludo, has said supporting President Bola Tinubu’s second-term bid could pave the way for an Igbo presidency in the future. In a video that circulated on X at the weekend, Soludo, speaking in Igbo, said backing Tinubu in the 2027 election could encourage other regions to support an Igbo presidential candidate when power returns to the South. He said the South-east should support the incumbent southern president, noting that power would shift to the north after Tinubu’s tenure before eventually returning to the south. “You have to engage in discussions. Now that it is a southerner holding the power; it’s remaining four years. It is now left for us (Igbos) to support him so that when it goes to the North and comes back, we can now trust that every southerner and northerner will support us,” he said. The governor said political power should rotate among different groups, adding that he had no intention of seeking a third term. “What am I vying for? I’ve gotten a governorship position; will I go for a third term? Everyone must be given the opportunity to be able to rise,” he said. Soludo also said the All Progressives Grand Alliance (APGA), the party under which he was elected governor, would support the prevailing political direction in the interest of the south-east. “As for APGA, we will support the moving train because that is where we can get our share that we would bring home in our own interest,” he said. His remarks followed his appointment to the revised presidential campaign council of the All Progressives Congress (APC), unveiled recently. Soludo was appointed to the council alongside Osun State governor, Ademola Adeleke, and the Minister of Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike. APGA described the governor’s inclusion as a testament to his consistent advocacy for a strategic partnership between Anambra State and the federal government for the collective good of Ndi Anambra and Ndigbo at large. In a statement, APGA’s National Publicity Secretary, Ejimofor Opera, said the partnership had yielded tangible benefits for Anambra, including federal collaboration on critical infrastructure projects and economic development initiatives. https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/25/t.summary: Over the past month, the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, has intensified several meetings with Rivers State Governor Siminalayi Fubara and his supporters to consolidate reconciliation between their political camps ahead of the 2027 general election. The meeting, held at Fubara’s private residence in Port Harcourt, came barely two weeks after political leaders loyal to both men met at the same venue.
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/25/t.summary_zh: 过去一个月，联邦首都 territories 部长 Nyesom Wike 加强了与 Rivers 州州长 Siminalayi Fubara 及其支持者的多次会晤，以在2027年大选前巩固两个政治阵营之间的和解。这次会晤在 Port Harcourt 的 Fubara 私人住所举行，距离忠于两人的政治领袖在同一地点会面仅有两周左右。
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/25/t.body: Over the past month, the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, has intensified several meetings with Rivers State Governor Siminalayi Fubara and his supporters to consolidate reconciliation between their political camps ahead of the 2027 general election. But will the rapprochement work? Davidson Iriekpen asks I t won’t be wrong to describe the current situation between the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Nyesom Wike, and the Governor of Rivers State, Siminalayi Fubara, as a case of the rejected stone emerging as the cornerstone. With Wike’s recent meetings with the governor, one can only deduce that the powerful minister is eating the humbling pie by his moves to get Fubara to play a crucial role in the Rainbow Coalition he set up to reelect President Bola Tinubu and install Kingsley Chinda as governor in 2027. The latest sign of Wike’s desperation was seen in the past week when the minister again led members of the State House of Assembly and the 23 local government chairmen in the state to a fresh meeting with the governor in continuation of the efforts to consolidate reconciliation between both political camps. The Speaker of the Rivers State House of Assembly, Martin Amaewhule, and the All Progressives Congress (APC) governorship candidate in the state, Chinda, were among those who accompanied Wike to the meeting. The meeting, held at Fubara’s private residence in Port Harcourt, came barely two weeks after political leaders loyal to both men met at the same venue. At the meeting, Wike urged supporters of Fubara to mobilise voters and ensure the state ranks among the top three states with the highest votes for President Tinubu in the 2027 elections. He said a strong electoral performance for Tinubu would position the South-south state for more federal appointments, infrastructure development and greater political influence at the national level. “All I want to hear in this state is Tinubu and nothing but Tinubu. If we play the role we are playing now, and we are one of the first three states that get the highest number of votes, we will get more of the appointments,” he said. The 2027 presidential election particularly, means a lot to Wike. Recall that recently, he public declared why Tinubu must win the poll because, according him, if Atiku Abubakar or Peter Obi wins the election, they would come after him. To understand why the minister’s latest move has caught critics’ attention one has to trace the origin of the political feud between him and Fubara. They once had a godfather and godson relationship until Fubara decided to be a man in control of his government and not another stooge. What he however didn’t anticipate was the power that Wike wields. Wike, who is no ordinary godfather, went to great lengths to humiliate the governor. Their disagreement, which began shortly after Fubara assumed office in 2023, triggered a protracted political crisis that divided the Rivers State House of Assembly. Tensions escalated in October 2023, when a fire incident damaged part of the assembly complex amid the dispute between both camps. Lawmakers loyal to Wike subsequently initiated impeachment proceedings against Fubara, deepening the confrontation between the executive and legislative arms of government. The crisis eventually led President Tinubu to declare a six-month emergency in Rivers State in March 2025, resulting in the suspension of the governor, his deputy and members of the state assembly. Wike had recently announced an end to the feud, saying Fubara had agreed to return to the political family that supported his emergence as governor. This was the same governor he made sure that the APC screened out of the ruling party’s primary election, forcing him to withdraw from the race. Chinda subsequently emerged as the APC’s sole candidate for the governorship election. Therefore, it is so ironic that the same FCT minister is desperately in need of Fubara, whom he had repeatedly denigrated and attempted to remove from office on many occasions. Last Monday, the intense troubleshooting efforts by Wike with Fubara continued, with the state assembly reversing its earlier decision to declare the seats of three lawmakers who supported the state governor vacant. At the assembly’s sitting, the 27 lawmakers led by Amaewhule resolved not only to rescind its threat against the Fubara-backed lawmakers, but to readmit them within their fold. This is a decision seen as critical to the peace process, which has since begun between the two camps. The pro-Fubara lawmakers, whose seats were earlier marked to be declared vacant, included Victor Oko-Jumbo, representing Bonny Constituency; Sokari Goodboy Sokari, Ahoada West; and Orubienimigha Timothy, Opobo/Nkoro Constituency. The assembly’s decision followed letters dated October 16, 2026 from the three lawmakers, which were read on the floor of the assembly during plenary. In the letter, the lawmakers requested that they be called back into the assembly to continue their legislative duties. It would be recalled that the assembly had, on October 30, 2023, in the heat of the political crisis, suspended the three lawmakers alongside Hon. Edison Ehie for alleged misconduct. Ehie, who later became the Chief of Staff to the governor, had resigned his membership of the assembly in the heat of the crisis, allowing for a by-election in his constituency. The trio’s suspension was, however, lifted on December 20, 2023, after the first peace meeting initiated by President Tinubu between Wike and Governor Fubara. But following the failure of the three lawmakers to attend sittings after their suspension was lifted, their seats were then declared vacant on October 15, 2025, by the Amaewhule-led assembly in line with section 109 sub 1 (e) of the Constitution. The assembly had consequently written to the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to conduct a by-election to fill the vacant seats. But during last Monday’s plenary, Speaker Amaewhule read the letters from each of the three lawmakers explaining that they never saw the letter lifting their suspension earlier, which was the reason they didn’t attend the sitting and appealed for the House to rescind its decision. The assembly’s decision might not be unconnected with Sunday’s meeting between Wike, the lawmakers, Chairmen of Local Government Areas and other leaders of the coalition with Governor Fubara and members of his team. The lingering question, however, is: Can Fubara genuinely reconcile with a man who, on many occasions, publicly denigrated and humiliated him, attempted to impeach him, instigated his suspension for six months, denied him a second term in office, replaced his local government officials, and denied his loyalists tickets to contest House of Assembly seats? Political analysts believe this is a delicate path to reconciliation – one that the governor must be strategic about and tread smartly. There is no doubt that the peace talks are largely driven by Wike’s political interests, particularly now that he has been assigned to lead President Tinubu’s re-election campaign. They may also be aimed at limiting the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC)’s impact on the presidential and governorship elections in Rivers. How this will pan out, however, remains to be seen. If Fubara accepts the olive branch and supports Wike’s campaign, some may interpret his actions as a sign of weakness. But if he plays his cards well, he could emerge with more than one political victory. https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/9199.title: Winners emerge in NCDMB Essay Competition
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/9199.summary: There were some 5,000 entries in the Essay Competition from 52 universities across the six geopolitical zones of the country, with consolation prizes going to the 4th to 9th place winners.
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/9199.summary_zh: 全国六个地缘政治区的52所大学共提交了约5000篇散文比赛参赛作品，第四至第九名获得安慰奖。
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/9199.body: The coveted prize of N1 million, a brand-new laptop and a plaque was won by Mr Wisdom David Fabunmi, a 200-level Physiotherapy student of the University of Ilorin, Kwara State, who emerged as overall winner, while the second prize of N700,000, laptop and plaque was won by Ms. Joy Oghogho Enogieru, a 100-level Doctor of Optometry student of the University of Benin, the first runner-up. The third prize of N500,000, laptop and a plaque was won by Mr. Ahmadu Kodan Yusuf, a 100-level Law student of Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria. There were some 5,000 entries in the Essay Competition from 52 universities across the six geopolitical zones of the country, with consolation prizes going to the 4th to 9th place winners. Representing the Executive Secretary of the NCDMB, Felix Omatsola Ogbe, at the Grand Finale of the Award and Prize-giving Ceremony, the General Manager, Corporate Communications Division (CCD), Dr. Obinna Ezeobi, stated that the competition is particularly important to the Board because it contributes to the realisation of its mandate, which centres on development of human and material capacity and monitoring of compliance by players in the oil and gas industry. Ezeobi pointed out that universities are institutions where ideas should be developed, problems examined, innovations encouraged and solutions created for the advancement of the society, hence the Board undertook to engage students and encourage them to think critically and write about Nigerian Content. The ideas, commitment and ingenuity of youths, he noted, were crucial to the future of Nigerian Content. He also listed the Nigerian Engineering Olympiad (NEO), to inspire innovation among engineering students, with the maiden edition concluded in July 2026. Ezeobi noted that the focus of this year’s essay competition on promoting manufacturing for sustainable local content development is intended to challenge participants to examine how Nigeria can strengthen its productive capacity and create greater economic value. According to him, “It is also the reason we implement a policy known as Nigerian Content Equipment Commitment (NCEC), which compels companies to show proof that they manufacture components and have capacity to execute key activities” before they get contract opportunities in the oil and gas industry. In his opening remarks, the Chairman of the occasion, Professor Promise Mebine, Vice Chancellor, Federal University, Otuoke, congratulated the NCDMB on its successful hosting and sponsorship of the competition and for staying faithful to the vision. “Year after year, you have proven that building Nigerian Content is not only about pipelines and platforms, but about building people, particularly our youths, the leaders of tomorrow,” he stated. To the winners, his word was, “Your prize today is well-deserved, but the real prize is not the cheque or the plaque. The real prize is that NCDMB has now opened a door for you. Walk through it!” To the other contestants, he said, “you are not losers; every essay you submitted is a seed. You have trained your mind to think. You have trained your hand to write. Keep writing; keep researching; keep believing in Nigeria; Next year, the podium may be yours.” In a goodwill message, the Director, Monitoring and Evaluation Directorate (MED) Mr. Esueme Dan Kikile, Esq. commended the Executive Secretary, the Corporate Communications Division and the programme consultant for all the effort toward sustenance of the competition, which he noted has been immensely beneficial to the Board and participants
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/9199.title_zh: 尼日利亚本地内容开发与监督委员会论文比赛揭晓获奖者
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/9199.body_zh: 人人梦寐以求的N1百万大奖、一台全新笔记本电脑和一块奖牌由Kwara State伊洛林大学200级物理治疗学学生Wisdom David Fabunmi先生夺得，他成为总得主；N700,000、笔记本电脑和奖牌组成的二等奖由University of Benin 100级验光学博士学生Joy Oghogho Enogieru女士获得，她荣膺亚军。N500,000、笔记本电脑和奖牌组成的三等奖由扎里亚Ahmadu Bello大学100级法学学生Ahmadu Kodan Yusuf先生获得。本次散文比赛共收到来自全国六个地缘政治区52所大学的约5,000份参赛作品，第四至第九名得主分别获得安慰奖。在颁奖与奖品授予仪式总决赛上，尼日利亚本地内容开发与监督委员会执行秘书Felix Omatsola Ogbe的发言代表、公司传播部门（CCD）总经理Dr. Obinna Ezeobi表示，这项比赛对委员会尤其重要，因为它有助于落实委员会以开发人力和物力能力、监测石油和天然气行业从业者合规情况为核心的职责。Ezeobi指出，大学是应当培育思想、审视问题、鼓励创新并创造解决方案、推动社会进步的机构，因此委员会着手与学生互动，鼓励他们批判性思考并撰写有关尼日利亚本地内容的文章。他指出，青年的创意、投入和 ingenuity对尼日利亚本地内容的未来至关重要。他还列举了旨在启发工程专业学生创新的尼日利亚工程奥林匹克（NEO），首届赛事已于2026年7月结束。Ezeobi表示，今年散文比赛聚焦于通过制造业促进可持续本地内容发展，意在促使参赛者思考尼日利亚如何增强生产能力并创造更大的经济价值。他说：“这也是我们推行一项名为尼日利亚本地内容设备承诺（NCEC）的政策的原因。该政策要求企业在获得石油和天然气行业的合同机会之前，提供证据证明其能够制造零部件，并具备执行关键活动的能力。”在开幕致辞中，活动主席、Federal University, Otuoke校长Promise Mebine教授祝贺尼日利亚本地内容开发与监督委员会成功举办并赞助本次比赛，并始终秉持既定愿景。他表示：“你们年复一年地证明，发展尼日利亚本地内容不仅是建设管道和平台，更在于培养人才，尤其是培养我们的青年——他们是未来的领导者。”他向获奖者表示：“你们今天获得的奖品实至名归，但真正的奖品不是支票或奖牌。真正的奖品是，尼日利亚本地内容开发与监督委员会现在已为你们打开了一扇门。迈过去吧！”他对其他参赛者说：“你们不是失败者；你们提交的每篇文章都是一颗种子。你们训练了自己的思维去思考，也训练了自己的双手去书写。继续写下去；继续研究；继续相信尼日利亚；明年，领奖台可能就是你们的。”在致辞中，监测与评估局（MED）局长Esueme Dan Kikile先生律师赞扬了执行秘书、公司传播部门和项目顾问为维持本次比赛作出的努力，并指出，这项比赛为委员会和参赛者带来了巨大益处

https://www.myjoyonline.com/mahama-links.body: President John Mahama says the struggle for control of Africa’s natural resources and the profits from their extraction are central to the continent’s security crises, warning that powerful interests benefit from prolonged instability. Addressing the 12th Tana High-Level Forum on Peace in Africa in Bahir Dar, Ethiopia, President Mahama said Africa, the President said the continent risks remaining vulnerable if its leaders fail to take greater control of their resources and determine their own security priorities. He said “Let me be clear, Africa is not an empty chessboard for foreign powers to play their games. We are not spectators,” he said. President Mahama said the importance of African minerals to the global green energy transition and digital economy should give the continent greater bargaining power, but communities endowed with these resources often bear the consequences of exploitation without enjoying the benefits. He argued that sovereignty must go beyond political independence and membership of international institutions. “Real sovereignty means having the administrative, legal, and economic power to govern your strategic assets, negotiate fair terms, and ensure the wealth beneath our people's feet actually puts food on their tables,” he said. He added that anything less amounted to “cosmetic independence that masks economic subjugation.” He says African leaders must look beyond weapons proliferation and military operations to confront the political and economic interests that sustain conflicts across the continent. “The real disease is mostly in the arena of political economy,” President Mahama said when presenting the 2026 State of Peace and Security in Africa Report at the 12th Tana High-Level Forum on Peace in Africa in Bahir Dar, Ethiopia. He challenged leaders to examine who controls natural resources, who benefits financially from their extraction and whose political and financial interests are better served by continued instability than lasting peace. “In every single theatre of conflict across this continent today, if you want to understand why guns are firing, do not start by counting the rifles,” he said. “Ask three basic questions, who controls the resource? Who cashes the cheque from its extraction? And whose political and financial fortunes are better served by perpetual chaos than by stable peace?” President Mahama cited Sudan, the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), Somalia and Mozambique as examples of how resource competition, governance failures and economic marginalisation contribute to insecurity. In Sudan, he said, the battle lines were drawn as much around gold extraction sites as around Khartoum. In eastern DRC, he linked the resurgence and entrenchment of the M23 group to coltan, cobalt and the global competition for minerals needed for the green energy transition. He also attributed the continued presence of Al-Shabaab in Somalia partly to governance failures that have created openings for the group to exploit. In Mozambique’s Cabo Delgado region, he said, the area’s substantial gas wealth has not translated into meaningful benefits for local young people, who instead viewed it as another source of marginalisation. “These are not separate, random brushfires. They are symptoms of a single, continent-wide firestorm,” he said

https://www.myjoyonline.com/mahama-links.body_zh: 约翰·马哈马总统表示，围绕非洲自然资源控制权及其开采利润的斗争，是非洲大陆安全危机的核心因素，并警告称，强大的利益集团正从长期动荡中获益。在埃塞俄比亚巴赫达尔举行的第12届塔纳非洲和平高级论坛上，马哈马总统指出，如果非洲领导人未能更好地掌控本国资源、确定自身的安全优先事项，非洲大陆仍可能处于脆弱状态。他说：“让我明确一点，非洲不是外国强权用来玩弄权术的空白棋盘。我们并非旁观者。”马哈马总统表示，非洲矿产对全球绿色能源转型和数字经济至关重要，这应当赋予非洲大陆更大的议价能力，但拥有这些资源的社区往往承受剥削带来的后果，却无法享受相关收益。他主张，主权不能仅仅意味着政治独立和加入国际组织。“真正的主权意味着拥有行政、法律和经济权力来治理自身的战略资产、谈判公平条件，并确保我们人民脚下的财富确实能够转化为餐桌上的食物。”他说。他补充称，低于这一标准的做法无异于“掩饰经济从属地位的表面独立”。他说，非洲领导人必须超越武器扩散和军事行动，正视维持非洲大陆各地冲突的政治和经济利益。马哈马总统在埃塞俄比亚巴赫达尔举行的第12届塔纳非洲和平高级论坛上发布《2026年非洲和平与安全状况报告》时表示：“真正的疾病主要存在于政治经济领域。”他敦促各国领导人审视谁在控制自然资源、谁从资源开采中获取经济利益，以及谁的政治和财政利益更能从持续动荡而非持久和平中获益。“在当今非洲大陆的每一个冲突地区，如果你想了解枪炮为何开火，不要从清点步枪数量开始。”他说，“要问三个根本问题：谁控制资源？谁从资源开采中拿到收益？谁的政治和财富状况更能从永久混乱而非稳定和平中获益？”马哈马总统列举苏丹、刚果民主共和国（DRC）、索马里和莫桑比克为例，说明资源竞争、治理失败和经济边缘化如何加剧不安全局势。在苏丹，他说，围绕黄金开采点的战线与围绕喀土穆的战线同样明显。在刚果民主共和国东部，他指出，M23组织东山再起和势力巩固与钶钽矿、钴以及全球对绿色能源转型所需矿产的竞争有关。他还称，治理失败为青年党在索马里扩大影响和牟取利益创造了空间 partly，这也是青年党继续存在的原因之一。他说，在莫桑比克的德尔加多岛地区，当地丰富的天然气财富并未给当地年轻人带来切实好处，反而被视为另一种边缘化来源。“这些并非彼此孤立、随机出现的零星冲突。它们是一场席卷整个大陆的单一风暴的症状。”他说

https://www.premiumtimesng.com/regional/.body: The Minister of State for Petroleum Resources (Gas), Ekperikpe Ekpo, has declared that the federal, state and local governments will combine their powers to secure overwhelming electoral victories for the APC in Akwa Ibom State, raising questions about the neutrality of public institutions ahead of the 2027 elections. Mr Ekpo made the declaration at a political rally in Etim Ekpo Local Government Area of Akwa Ibom State, where he introduced the APC candidate for the Akwa Ibom State House of Assembly constituency. “This State Constituency, this Federal Constituency, this Senatorial District, this Akwa Ibom State is going to be 100 over 100. I can tell you that as a federal minister,” he told the crowd at the rally. “We will bring federal might and join with state might and join with local government might and make sure the people of this local government, whether you like that blessing, that blessing will come to you. A man of peace is on the throne.” The minister did not explain what he meant by combining the powers of the three tiers of government or how the proposed mobilisation would be carried out. His remarks drew attention to longstanding concerns surrounding the use of government power and public resources to influence electoral outcomes in Nigeria, where political expressions such as “federal might” have often fuelled suspicions of possible interference in the electoral process. Under Nigeria’s democratic architecture, elections are expected to provide a level playing field for political parties and candidates, while public institutions must operate within the law rather than serve the electoral interests of the party in power. Mr Ekpo’s spokesperson, Louis Ibah, did not respond to a media enquiry sent to him on WhatsApp on Friday, despite reading the message. A reminder sent on Saturday morning and a subsequent telephone call also went unanswered. In the enquiry, PREMIUM TIMES asked Mr Ibah to clarify what the minister meant by combining federal, state and local government power in the election and how the declaration aligned with democratic competition and the neutrality of public institutions. Mr Ekpo’s remarks follow concerns about political leaders making declarations that appear to presume electoral results before voters cast their ballots. In September, PREMIUM TIMES reported that Emmanuel Enoidem, a chieftain of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Akwa Ibom and a Senior Advocate of Nigeria, insisted that a federal lawmaker, Clement Jimbo, would be returned to the House of Representatives in 2027, “whether you like it or not”. Mr Enoidem made the declaration while soliciting support for Mr Jimbo, who represents Abak/Etim Ekpo/Ika Federal Constituency. Some members of the audience reportedly rejected the appeal. Mr Enoidem subsequently told PREMIUM TIMES that his remarks were directed at APC members, arguing that party members were expected to support their party’s candidates. He also acknowledged the right of voters to freely choose their preferred candidates. Mr Ekpo’s expression steered political discourse in Akwa Ibom, invoking concerns about whether the machinery of government could be used to influence electoral competition in the 2027 general elections. Mr Ekpo’s declaration is particularly noteworthy because he occupies a federal executive position and noted that he speaks from the hindsight of being a minister while openly invoking the use of federal powers for an electoral result. Although political parties and their members are entitled to campaign for electoral victories, using public office or government institutions to confer an unfair advantage on a party would raise serious questions about electoral integrity. Nigeria’s constitution guarantees citizens the right to participate in government, while the Electoral Act provides the legal framework for conducting elections. The credibility of the process depends, in part, on voters being able to make their choices freely, without intimidation or improper interference. Mr Ekpo did not explicitly threaten violence in the remarks reviewed by PREMIUM TIMES. However, his reference to combining federal, state and local government “might,” coupled with his revelation that he is speaking based on his privileged position as a “federal minister,” raises questions about the means through which he intends to secure the sweeping electoral victory he predicted. Until he clarifies his remarks, that question remains unanswered
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/regional/.title_zh: 2027年：部长威胁在阿夸伊博姆选举中动用“联邦力量”
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/regional/.body_zh: 尼日利亚联邦政府石油资源（天然气）国务部长埃克佩里克·埃克波宣布，联邦、州和地方政府将合力，确保全进步大会党（APC）在阿夸伊博姆州取得压倒性选举胜利；此举引发外界对2027年选举前公共机构中立性的质疑。埃克波在阿夸伊博姆州埃廷·埃克波地方政府辖区的一场政治集会上发表上述声明，并在会上为阿夸伊博姆州众议院选区的APC候选人站台。他说：“这个州选区、这个联邦选区、这个参议员选区、整个阿夸伊博姆州都将以百分之百对百分之百的得票获胜。作为联邦部长，我可以向你们保证这一点。”他告诉集会人群：“我们将调动联邦力量，与州政府力量和地方政府力量汇合，确保这个地方政府的人民都能得到那份祝福；无论你们是否愿意接受，这份祝福都会降临到你们身上。和平之人将坐上王座。”这位部长没有解释他所说的三级政府力量合是什么意思，也没有说明拟议中的动员将如何实施。他的言论使人们再次关注尼日利亚围绕利用政府权力和公共资源影响选举结果的长期争议。在尼日利亚，“联邦力量”等政治言论常常加深外界对选举进程可能受到干预的疑虑。按照尼日利亚的民主制度，选举应当为政党和候选人提供公平竞争环境，而公共机构必须依法运作，不能服务于执政党的选举利益。PREMIUM TIMES于星期五通过WhatsApp向埃克波的发言人路易斯·伊巴发送媒体问询，但伊巴读后仍未回复。星期六上午发出的提醒以及随后拨打的电话也未获回应。在问询中，PREMIUM TIMES请伊巴澄清部长所说的在选举中合并联邦、州和地方政府力量具体意味着什么，以及这一声明如何符合民主竞争要求和公共机构中立性原则。此前已有关于政治人士提前宣布似乎预设选举结果的担忧。9月，PREMIUM TIMES报道称，阿夸伊博姆州全进步大会党（APC）高层、尼日利亚资深大律师埃马纽埃尔·埃诺伊德姆坚称，联邦议员克莱门特·金博无论人们是否愿意，都将在2027年再次当选众议员。埃诺伊德姆在为金博争取支持时作出这番声明。金博代表阿巴克/埃廷·埃克波/伊卡联邦选区。据报道，部分现场听众拒绝响应这一呼吁。埃诺伊德姆随后告诉PREMIUM TIMES，他的讲话是面向APC党员的，并称党员理应支持本党候选人。他还承认选民有权自由选择中意的候选人。埃克波的这番表态影响了阿夸伊博姆州的政治讨论，并再次引发人们关注政府机器能否被用于左右2027年大选中的选举竞争。埃克波的声明尤其值得注意，因为他担任联邦行政职务，并指出自己是以“联邦部长”的特殊身份说这番话，同时公开主张动用联邦力量来实现选举结果。尽管政党及其成员有权为赢得选举开展竞选，但利用公职或政府机构为某一政党赋予不公平优势，将引发对选举诚信的严重质疑。尼日利亚宪法保障公民参与政府的权利，《选举法》则为选举的举行提供法律框架。选举进程的可信度部分取决于选民能否在没有恐吓或不当干预的情况下自由作出选择。在PREMIUM TIMES审阅的言论中，埃克波并未明确威胁使用暴力。然而，他提到要合并联邦、州和地方政府的“力量”，并透露自己凭借“联邦部长”的特殊身份发表这番话，这使人们产生疑问：他究竟打算通过何种手段，确保自己预测的这场压倒性选举胜利？在他澄清这些言论之前，这一问题仍无答案。

https://www.myjoyonline.com/cagg-demands.summary: In a press release dated October 24, 2026, the coalition condemned the reported remarks, describing them as unlawful and reckless, and warning that they could undermine efforts to combat illegal mining, popularly known as galamsey. The coalition therefore wants the GoldBod CEO to immediately retract the alleged statement and issue an unqualified apology to the Ghanaian public.
https://www.myjoyonline.com/cagg-demands.summary_zh: 在一份日期为2026年10月24日的新闻稿中，该联盟谴责了有关言论，称其违法且鲁莽，并警告称，这些言论可能破坏打击俗称 galamsey 的非法采矿的努力。因此，该联盟要求 GoldBod 首席执行官立即撤回被指称的声明，并向加纳公众作出无保留的道歉。
https://www.myjoyonline.com/cagg-demands.body: The Ghana Coalition Against Galamsey (CAGG) has called on the Office of the Attorney-General to investigate the Chief Executive Officer of the Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod) over statements it claims encouraged artisanal miners to operate without licences, provided they avoid forest reserves and river bodies. In a press release dated October 24, 2026, the coalition condemned the reported remarks, describing them as unlawful and reckless, and warning that they could undermine efforts to combat illegal mining, popularly known as galamsey. CAGG argued that Ghana's mining laws do not exempt miners from licensing requirements based on the location of their operations. Citing Section 99(2)(a) of the Minerals and Mining Act, 2006 (Act 703), as amended by Act 995 of 2019, the coalition said anyone who undertakes mining without a licence granted by the Minister commits an offence. It further cited Section 99, arguing that anyone who commands, instigates, employs or facilitates others to engage in illegal mining could face the same penalties as the illegal miner. According to the coalition, offenders could face fines ranging from GH¢120,000 to GH¢180,000 and imprisonment of between 15 and 25 years, or both. The coalition therefore wants the GoldBod CEO to immediately retract the alleged statement and issue an unqualified apology to the Ghanaian public. It has also urged President John Dramani Mahama, the Minister for Lands and Natural Resources, and the Minerals Commission to publicly reaffirm that mining without a licence is illegal, regardless of where the activity takes place. CAGG further called on the Attorney-General's Office to investigate the matter for possible abetment of illegal mining, insisting that no individual should be exempt from the law. Beyond the legal implications, the coalition warned that the reported remarks could expose farmers and landowners to encroachment on their lands. It has consequently called on the Ministry of National Security, the Ghana Police Service and the Ministry of the Interior to strengthen protection for farmers and landowners and establish rapid-response channels for reporting encroachment. The group is also demanding a clear national plan to protect farmlands, including legal safeguards for agricultural lands, mapping and registration of farms, support for vulnerable farmers seeking to document their land rights, and compensation and restoration for those whose lands have been destroyed. CAGG said GoldBod was established to formalise and regulate artisanal mining, not to encourage unlicensed operations. It warned that normalising mining without licences would weaken the regulatory framework intended to distinguish legal small-scale mining from illegal mining. The coalition comprises civil society organisations, professional associations, environmental advocacy groups and other stakeholders
https://www.myjoyonline.com/cagg-demands.title_zh: CAGG要求加纳黄金局首席执行官撤回涉嫌支持非法采矿的言论并道歉
https://www.myjoyonline.com/cagg-demands.body_zh: 加纳反非法采矿联盟（CAGG）呼吁总检察长办公室调查加纳黄金局（GoldBod）首席执行官，因为该联盟声称，此人的言论鼓励手工采矿者在不办理许可证的情况下开采，只需避开森林保护区和河流即可。在日期为2026年10月24日的新闻公报中，该联盟谴责了据报道的相关言论，称其违法且鲁莽，并警告称，这些言论可能削弱打击俗称“galamsey”的非法采矿活动的努力。CAGG认为，加纳的采矿法律并未根据采矿活动的地点免除采矿者办理许可证的要求。该联盟援引经2019年第995号法案修订的《2006年矿产与采矿法》（第703号法案）第99(2)(a)条，称任何人在未获得部长颁发许可证的情况下从事采矿，均构成违法行为。该联盟还援引第99条，认为任何指使、煽动、雇用或协助他人从事非法采矿的人，都可能与非法采矿者面临同样的处罚。据该联盟称，违法者可能被处以GH¢120,000至GH¢180,000的罚款，并处以15年至25年监禁，或两者并处。因此，该联盟要求GoldBod首席执行官立即收回据称发表的言论，并不加保留地向加纳公众道歉。该联盟还敦促约翰·德拉马尼·马哈马总统、土地与自然资源部长以及矿产委员会公开重申，无论采矿活动在哪里进行，无许可证采矿均属违法。CAGG进一步呼吁总检察长办公室调查此事，审查是否构成对非法采矿的协助，并坚持任何个人都不应免于法律制裁。除法律影响外，该联盟警告称，据报道的相关言论可能使农民和土地所有者面临土地被侵占的问题。因此，该联盟呼吁国家安全部、加纳警察局和内政部加强对农民和土地所有者的保护，并建立快速响应渠道，以便报告土地侵占事件。该团体还要求制定明确的全国农地保护计划，包括为农业土地提供法律保障、绘制并登记农场、协助弱势农民确认土地权利，以及对土地遭到破坏者给予赔偿并协助恢复土地。CAGG表示，设立GoldBod是为了使手工采矿正规化并加强监管，而不是鼓励无证经营。该联盟警告称，将无许可证采矿正常化会削弱旨在区分合法小规模采矿与非法采矿的监管框架。该联盟由民间社会组织、专业协会、环保倡议团体及其他利益相关方组成
